Anna likes to make things with paper and scissors. She has many colors of paper, but her favorite is green. She likes to cut green paper into different shapes and stick them on the wall.

One day, she finds a book with many patterns in it. She sees a pattern of a flower with five petals and a circle in the middle. She thinks it is very pretty and wants to make it with green paper.

She asks her mom for help. "Mom, can you help me cut this pattern?" she says, showing her the book.

"Sure, Anna, I can help you. But first, we need to trace the pattern on the paper. Do you have a pencil?" her mom says.

Anna nods and runs to get a pencil. She comes back with a green pencil and a green paper. She puts the paper on the table and opens the book. She puts the pencil on the pattern and moves it along the lines. She makes a mark on the paper that looks like the pattern.

"Good job, Anna. Now we can cut the paper along the marks. Do you have your scissors?" her mom says.

Anna nods again and gets her scissors. She holds the paper with one hand and the scissors with the other. She cuts the paper carefully, following the marks. She makes a green flower with five petals and a circle in the middle.

"Wow, Anna, you did a great job. Your flower is very beautiful. Where do you want to stick it?" her mom says.

Anna smiles and looks at the wall. She sees a spot that is empty. She says, "I want to stick it there. It will make the wall more pretty."

She gets some tape and sticks the flower on the wall. She steps back and admires her work. She is very happy and proud. She says, "Thank you, mom, for helping me. I love my green flower."

Her mom hugs her and says, "You're welcome, Anna. I love your green flower too. And I love you more."

Sam and Ben are brothers. They like to play with their toys. Sam has a red motorcycle. Ben has a blue car. They make noises and race on the floor.

"Look at my motorcycle!" Sam says. "It is fast and loud. Vroom, vroom!"

"My car is faster and louder!" Ben says. "Beep, beep!"

They zoom their toys around the room. They have fun.

Then, Mom comes in. She has a big smile. She holds a paper in her hand.

"Boys, I have something to show you," she says. "I passed my test. I can drive a real motorcycle now!"

Sam and Ben stop playing. They look at Mom. They are surprised.

"A real motorcycle?" Sam asks. "Like my toy?"

"Yes, like your toy, but bigger and stronger," Mom says. "Do you want to see it?"

Sam and Ben nod. They follow Mom outside. They see a shiny black motorcycle parked on the street. Mom puts on a helmet and gloves. She sits on the motorcycle. She turns it on. It makes a loud noise. Vroom, vroom!

Sam and Ben clap their hands. They are excited.

"Wow, Mom, you are cool!" Sam says.

"Yeah, Mom, you are awesome!" Ben says.

Mom smiles. She is proud. She hugs Sam and Ben.

"Thank you, boys," she says. "You are cool and awesome too. Do you want to go for a ride with me?"

Sam and Ben look at each other. They shrug. They don't know what to say. They are a little scared of the big motorcycle. But they also want to try something new.

"Okay, Mom," they say. "We will go with you. But be careful!"

Mom laughs. She puts Sam and Ben in a sidecar. She buckles them up. She gives them helmets and gloves too. She says, "Don't worry, boys. I will be careful. And we will have fun. Are you ready?"

Sam and Ben nod. They are ready. They hold Mom's hand. They make noises. Vroom, vroom! Beep, beep!

Mom drives the motorcycle. She goes slow and steady. She waves to the people on the street. They wave back. They think Mom and the boys are cool and awesome too.

Sam and Ben enjoy the ride. They see new things. They feel the wind. They laugh and smile.

They love Mom. They love the motorcycle. They are happy.

Sara and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to swing and slide and run. They saw a big dog with a red collar. The dog looked friendly and wagged its tail.

"Can we pet the dog?" Sara asked Tom.

"OK, but be careful," Tom said. They walked slowly to the dog and reached out their hands. The dog licked Sara's hand and sniffed Tom's hair. They giggled and stroked the dog's fur.

The dog's owner was a lady with a big hat and a long dress. She smelled like perfume. She saw Sara and Tom and got angry.

"Hey, get away from my dog!" she shouted. "He doesn't like strangers. He might bite you!"

Sara and Tom were frightened. They let go of the dog and ran back to the swings. The lady followed them and grabbed their arms.

"You naughty children! How dare you touch my dog without asking? I'm going to tell your parents and the police!" she said.

Sara and Tom cried and tried to get free. They wished their mom and dad were here. They did not know what to do. They felt very sad and scared. They sighed and hoped the lady would let them go. But she did not. She dragged them to her car and locked them inside. She drove away with the dog and the perfume. Sara and Tom never saw their parents again.

"Let's open it!" Tim said.

"No, we can't!" Jen said. "Mommy warned us not to touch the pot. It is hot and we can get hurt."

Tim did not listen to Jen. He was curious and brave. He climbed on a chair and reached for the pot. He grabbed the handle and pulled.

The pot was very heavy. It tipped over and spilled. Hot water and noodles came out. They splashed on Tim and Jen. They screamed and cried. It hurt a lot.

Mommy heard the noise and ran to the kitchen. She saw Tim and Jen on the floor. They were wet and red. She was angry and scared. She called for help.

"Tim and Jen, what did you do?" Mommy said. "I warned you not to touch the pot. Why didn't you listen to me?"

Tim and Jen were sorry. They said they were sorry. But it was too late. They had to go to the hospital. They had weird marks on their skin. They had to stay in bed for a long time. They learned their lesson. They never touched the pot again.

Timmy likes to look at the stars at night. He has a big book with pictures of stars and planets. He learns their names and colors. He wants to see them for real.

One night, he sees a bright light in the sky. It moves very fast and leaves a long tail. He runs to his mom and dad and says, "Look, look, a comet!"

His mom and dad smile and hug him. They say, "Yes, that's a comet, Timmy. It's very rare and special. Do you know what a comet is?"

Timmy shakes his head. He wants to know more.

His mom says, "A comet is a big ball of ice and dust that travels around the sun. Sometimes it comes close to the earth and we can see it. It's very beautiful, isn't it?"

Timmy nods. He thinks the comet is amazing. He says, "Can I touch it?"

His dad says, "No, Timmy, you can't touch it. It's very far away and very hot. But you can imagine it. You can pretend you are a space explorer and you fly to the comet. What would you do?"

Timmy thinks for a moment. He says, "I would say hello to the comet. I would ask it where it came from and where it is going. I would be nice and helpful. Maybe the comet is lonely and needs a friend."

His mom and dad laugh and kiss him. They say, "That's very sweet, Timmy. You are a good and kind boy. We are proud of you. And we are sure the comet would like you too."

Timmy smiles and hugs them. He says, "Thank you, mom and dad. I love you. And I love the comet too. Good night, comet. See you again."

He goes to his bed and dreams of the comet. He imagines he is flying with it in the sky. He is happy.

Lily and Ben nod. They do not want to lose the train. They say sorry to each other. They start to play with the train. They number the seats and make the train go fast and slow. They have fun. They are not bossy anymore.

Sam and Mia were twins who loved to play at the beach. They liked to build sand castles, look for shells and splash in the water. One day, they saw a big boat on the sea. It was white and shiny and had a flag on it.

"Wow, look at that boat!" Sam said. "It is so big and pretty. I want to go on it."

"No, Sam, we can't go on it," Mia said. "It is not our boat. It belongs to someone else. And the sea is too deep and powerful. It can hurt us if we go too far."

"But I want to see the boat, Mia. Please, let me go. Just for a little bit. I will be careful," Sam said. He did not listen to his sister. He ran to the water and started to swim towards the boat.

"Sam, come back!" Mia shouted. She was scared for her brother. She saw the waves getting bigger and stronger. She saw the boat moving away. She saw Sam getting tired and scared. She ran to get help.

A man who worked at the beach saw Mia and heard her cry. He had a small boat with a motor. He quickly got on the boat and went to the sea. He saw Sam and threw him a rope. He pulled Sam into the boat and took him back to the shore.

"Thank you, thank you, thank you!" Mia said. She hugged her brother and cried. She was happy he was safe.

"I'm sorry, Mia. I'm sorry, mister. I was silly and naughty. I should have listened to you. The sea is too powerful for me. I don't want to go on the big boat anymore. I just want to play with you," Sam said. He was sorry and ashamed. He learned his lesson.

The man smiled and said, "It's okay, Sam. I'm glad you are okay. But you have to be careful and listen to your sister. The sea can be fun, but it can also be dangerous. You have to respect it and stay close to the shore. And you have to ask before you go on someone else's boat. Do you understand?"

"Yes, I understand. Thank you for saving me. You are very kind and brave," Sam said.

"It's a special car that helps people who are hurt or sick," her mommy replied. 

Lily thought about this and decided she wanted to be a helper too. So, she put some of her pretty rocks in her pocket and went to find someone to help. 

She saw an old man who had fallen down and hurt his leg. Lily gave him her pretty rocks to make him feel better. But the old man was angry and shouted at her to leave him alone. Lily felt sad and confused. 

She went back home and told her mommy what happened. Her mommy explained that sometimes people are not feeling well and they don't want help. Lily learned that it's important to be kind, but also to listen to what people need.

Suddenly, a hurricane came and it was very strong. Timmy was scared and ran inside, but it was too late. The hurricane destroyed Timmy's house and he lost all of his toys. Timmy learned his lesson and promised to be a good boy from now on.

Max was happy to have helped the little kitten and they became good friends.

Ducky didn't listen and followed the alligator anyway. The alligator led Ducky to a place with lots of yummy food. But when Ducky tried to eat, the alligator snapped his big jaws and chased Ducky away.

Ducky realized that Mama Duck was right. It's not always safe to follow strangers, even if they lead you to something yummy. From then on, Ducky always listened to Mama Duck and stayed safe in the pond. The end.

To Timmy's surprise, the car started moving again! He was so happy that he fixed it all by himself. From that day on, Timmy knew that even when things seem broken, he could always try to fix them.

The bird was brown too, just like the penny. Lily and Timmy couldn't believe their eyes. They knew they had found something very special. From that day on, they always kept their eyes open for more brown pennies with surprises on them.

Once upon a time, there was an old man named Grandpa. He lived in a small house with his granddaughter, Lily. One day, Lily asked Grandpa, "What's a hurricane?" Grandpa replied, "A hurricane is a big, strong wind that can blow things away."

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise outside. Grandpa looked out the window and saw that a hurricane was coming! He quickly grabbed Lily's hand and they ran to the basement to stay safe. As they waited for the hurricane to pass, Grandpa told Lily stories about when he was a little boy.

After a while, the wind started to calm down and the hurricane passed. Grandpa and Lily went outside to see the damage. They saw that some trees had fallen down and there were leaves and branches everywhere. Grandpa said, "We're lucky that our house is okay. Let's clean up the yard together." And so, they spent the rest of the day picking up sticks and leaves, happy to be safe and together.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly around and play with his friends. One day, Tweety found a bright egg in his nest. He didn't know where it came from, but he knew it was special.

Tweety asked his friends if they knew anything about the egg, but they didn't reply. Tweety decided to take care of the egg all by himself. He sat on the egg and kept it warm with his feathers.

Days went by, and finally, the egg cracked open! Out came a little chick, just like Tweety. The chick looked up at Tweety and chirped happily. Tweety was so happy that he took care of the egg and now had a new friend to play with.

From that day on, Tweety and the little chick played together every day. They flew around and explored the world together. Tweety was so happy that he found the bright egg and took care of it. He knew that it was all worth it in the end.

Once upon a time, there was a big, bald eagle named Eddie. Eddie lived in a tree near a river. He loved to fly high in the sky and catch fish in the river. One day, Eddie saw a little rabbit named Benny trying to cross the river.

"Hello little rabbit, do you need help?" Eddie asked.

"Yes please, I can't swim very well," Benny replied.

Eddie flew down and picked up Benny with his strong talons. As they flew across the river, Benny noticed something shiny on Eddie's head.

"What's that on your head?" Benny asked.

"It's my bow," Eddie replied. "I wear it when I want to look fancy."

After they landed, Eddie put Benny down and they said goodbye. Benny hopped away, but he couldn't stop thinking about Eddie's bow. The next day, Benny went back to the river and found a shiny rock. He used his teeth to make it into a bow and wore it proudly.

They played together for a while, but then Timmy saw his friends playing on the other side of the park. He wanted to go play with them, but he didn't want to leave the little girl alone. So, he said, "Do you want to come with me and play with my friends?" 

The little girl nodded and they walked over to Timmy's friends. When they arrived, Timmy's friends were happy to see him and the little girl. They all played together and had a lot of fun. Timmy was happy that he didn't have to feel lonely anymore and that he could point his friends to his new friend.

Lily smiled and said, "I understand, but it takes time for your lung to get better. Just imagine you're breathing in fresh air from a big, beautiful garden. That will help you feel better."

Teddy closed his eyes and imagined the garden. He took deep breaths and felt his lung getting stronger. Soon, he was back to his happy self and thanked Lily for being such a good doctor.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and chase butterflies. One day, she was playing in the park when she saw a big, dark shadow on the ground. She looked up and saw a big bird flying high in the sky. 

Lily continued to play, but she couldn't stop thinking about the shadow. She wondered where it came from and why it was so big. As she played, she heard a sound. It was a ringing sound. She looked around and saw a man with a big bell. 

The man rang the bell and Lily knew it was time to go home. She ran back to her house and told her mom about the shadow and the ringing sound. Her mom explained that the shadow was from the bird and the ringing sound was from the man with the bell. Lily felt sorry for not understanding before, but she was happy to have learned something new. From that day on, she looked up at the sky and listened for the ringing sound whenever she saw a shadow.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear. The bear liked to sit under a big tree in the forest. One day, the bear saw a lumber truck drive by. The truck was carrying lots of big logs. The bear thought the logs looked regular and decided to go check them out. 

When the bear got to the logs, he saw that they were all different sizes. Some were long and some were short. The bear decided to sit on one of the logs. It was very hard and not comfortable at all. The bear decided to go back to his cozy spot under the tree and take a nap. 

From that day on, the bear would regularly sit under the tree and watch the lumber trucks drive by. He knew he didn't like sitting on the logs, but he still thought they looked interesting. And so, the bear continued to enjoy his regular routine in the forest.

When they arrived at the park, Max couldn't wait to play. He ran around and chased his ball until he got tired. Then, he saw a tree with flexible branches and decided to climb it. But, as he was climbing, he lost his balance and fell down.

Luckily, Max wasn't hurt and Lily was there to help him. She gave him a big hug and told him it was okay. Max learned that even when things don't go as planned, he can always count on his owner to be there for him.

As they walked around the museum, Lily saw many interesting things. She saw a big dinosaur skeleton and a shiny crown that a queen wore a long time ago. She loved looking at all the different things and learning about what happened a long time ago.

Suddenly, Lily saw a shiny vase that she really wanted to touch. Her mommy told her not to touch it because it was very old and could break easily. But Lily didn't listen and touched it anyway. The vase fell and broke into many pieces. Lily's mommy was very upset and they had to leave the museum. Lily learned that it's important to listen and not touch things that don't belong to us.

It was hard work, but the little bear was determined. He climbed and he climbed, until finally he reached the top of the tree! He was so happy that he made a loop. 

The little bear learned that determination and a little bit of rope can go a long way.

Lily was nervous because she didn't want to hurt the crab. She carefully poured the crab into the ocean and watched it swim away. Her mommy and daddy were proud of her for being so gentle with the crab.

Later that day, Lily and her family went to get ice cream. As they were walking, Lily saw a little boy crying because he dropped his ice cream. She remembered how nervous she was with the crab and decided to share her ice cream with the little boy. The little boy was happy and thanked Lily. Her mommy and daddy were proud of her again for being so kind.

Lily liked to wear her swan dress. It was white and soft and had a big swan on the front. She wore it every day, even when it was hot or cold. She did not want to wear any other dress.

One day, she went to the park with her mom and dad. They saw some real swans in the pond. Lily ran to them and said hello. She wanted to play with them. But the swans did not like Lily. They hissed and snapped at her. They thought she was trying to take their pond. Lily was scared and sad. She ran back to her mom and dad.

Her mom and dad hugged her and said, "Lily, the swans are not your friends. They are wild animals. They do not like to share their pond with anyone. They do not like your swan dress. It makes them angry. You should wear something else when you go to the park."

Lily did not want to hear that. She loved her swan dress. She said, "No, I want to wear my swan dress. It is my favorite. I do not care what the swans think."

Her mom and dad shook their heads. They said, "Lily, you are being stubborn and foolish. You are not respecting the swans or yourself. You are making yourself unhappy and unsafe. You should wear something that is good for the weather and the place. You have many other nice dresses. You can wear your swan dress at home or at a party. But not at the park."

Lily thought about what her mom and dad said. She looked at the swans in the pond. They looked calm and happy. She looked at her swan dress. It was white and soft and had a big swan on the front. But it was also hot and sticky and made the swans mad. She realized that her mom and dad were right. She said, "I'm sorry, mom and dad. You are right. I should wear something else at the park. I will wear my swan dress another time. Can we go home and change?"

Her mom and dad smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. We are proud of you. You are learning to be smart and kind. You are learning to wear what is best for you and others."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, mom and dad. I love you. And I love my swan dress. But I also love the swans. And I love myself."

The end.

Ben and Mia like to draw on pages. They have many pages in a big book. The book is cheap and old. Mom says they can draw on the book, but not on other things.

One day, Ben and Mia are bored. They want to draw something new. They look around the room. They see a shiny book on the shelf. The book has a picture of a dragon on the cover.

"Let's draw on that book!" Ben says.

"No, that is Dad's book. He likes it a lot. He will be mad if we draw on it." Mia says.

Ben does not listen. He takes the book from the shelf. He opens it. He sees many pages with words and pictures. He thinks they are boring. He wants to make them fun.

He takes a crayon. He starts to draw on a page. He draws a big red nose on a man. He laughs.

Mia sees what Ben is doing. She is scared. She tries to stop him.

"Ben, stop! You are ruining the book! Dad will be very sad and angry!" Mia says.

Ben does not stop. He likes to draw on the book. He thinks it is funny. He removes a page from the book. He tears it in half. He throws it on the floor.

Mia cries. She picks up the page. She tries to put it back in the book. She cannot. The page is broken.

Ben sees Mia crying. He does not care. He removes another page from the book. He draws on it. He tears it. He throws it.

Mia cries louder. She runs to the door. She calls for Mom.

"Mom, Mom, come quick! Ben is destroying Dad's book!" Mia shouts.

Mom hears Mia. She comes to the room. She sees the mess. She sees the book. She sees the pages. She is shocked. She is angry.

"Ben, what have you done? How could you do this? This is Dad's favorite book! It is very special and expensive! You are in big trouble, young man!" Mom yells.

Ben stops drawing. He looks at Mom. He sees her face. He is scared. He knows he did something bad. He tries to hide the crayon. He does not say anything.

Mom takes the book from Ben. She sees the damage. She is very sad. She knows Dad will be very sad too. She does not know how to fix the book.

She takes Ben by the hand. She drags him to his room. She puts him in the corner. She tells him to stay there until Dad comes home.

She leaves the room. She closes the door. She goes to Mia. She hugs her. She says she is sorry. She says she will try to make the book better.

Ben stays in the corner. He feels bad. He wishes he did not draw on the book. He wishes he listened to Mia. He wonders what Dad will do when he sees the book. He is afraid. He cries.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the forest near their home. The forest was deep and had many trees and animals. Sometimes they saw birds, squirrels, rabbits and deer. They liked to make up stories and pretend they were explorers or fairies or knights.

One day, they found a big rock with a hole in it. They looked inside and saw something shiny. It was a necklace with a blue stone. Lily wanted to try it on, but Ben said no. He said it might be magic and change them into something else. Lily did not believe him. She said it was just a pretty necklace and she wanted to wear it.

She took the necklace and put it around her neck. As soon as she did, she felt a strange feeling. She looked at Ben and saw that he was not Ben anymore. He was a frog! She tried to speak, but she could only make a croak. She looked at herself and saw that she was a frog too! The necklace had changed them!

They were scared and sad. They did not want to be frogs. They wanted to be children again. They tried to take off the necklace, but it was too tight. They hopped around the rock, hoping to find someone who could help them. But the forest was deep and quiet. They did not see anyone.

They did not know what to do. They wished they had listened to Ben and left the necklace alone. They wondered if they would ever be children again. They hugged each other and cried. They hoped that someone would find them and change them back.

"Let's open it and see," says Ben.

"No, don't do that. It might be dirty or smelly," says Sam.

But Ben does not listen. He runs to the bin and lifts the lid. He sees a lot of rubbish and flies. He also sees a banana peel. He thinks it is funny. He picks it up and throws it at Sam.

"Hey, stop that!" says Sam. He is angry and scared. He dodges the banana peel and runs away.

Ben laughs and chases him. He tries to throw more rubbish at him. He thinks it is a game.

Sam does not like this game. He frowns and cries. He runs to his mum and tells her what Ben did. His mum is not happy. She tells Ben's mum.

Ben's mum is not happy either. She tells Ben to stop and say sorry. She makes him pick up the rubbish and put it back in the bin. She says he has to be nice and gentle with his friend.

Ben feels bad. He is slow and sad. He says sorry to Sam and his mum. He says he will not do it again.

One day, they watched a movie about a famous man who could fly and had a big S on his shirt. Sam thought he was very cool and strong. He wanted to be like him when he grew up. He asked his dad many questions about the man and his powers.

"Can he fly to the moon?" Sam asked.

"Maybe, but he likes to stay on Earth and help people," his dad said.

"Can he lift a car?" Sam asked.

"Yes, he can lift anything. He's very strong," his dad said.

"Can he stop bad guys?" Sam asked.

"Of course, he's a hero. He always stops the bad guys," his dad said.

Sam watched the movie with wonder and excitement. He saw the man fly, lift, and stop many things. He cheered and clapped when the man saved the day.

But then, something happened. The movie stopped. The screen went black. Sam was confused and scared.

"Dad, what happened? Where's the man?" Sam cried.

His dad looked at the box and saw a red light. He realized what happened.

"Oh, no. The box ran out of power. We need to plug it in," his dad said.

He got up and looked for the cord. He found it behind the TV. He tried to plug it in, but it was too short. He needed to move the TV closer to the wall.

"Sam, can you help me?" his dad asked.

Sam nodded and got up. He went to the other side of the TV and pushed it with his dad. They moved it a little bit, but it was still too far.

"Sam, can you pause the movie?" his dad asked.

Sam looked at the box and saw a button with a symbol that looked like two fingers. He remembered that his dad told him that this button could pause the movie.

"OK, dad. I can pause the movie," Sam said.

He pressed the button and heard a click. The screen came back on, but the movie did not move. It was paused.

"Good job, Sam. You paused the movie. Now we can plug it in," his dad said.

He reached for the cord and plugged it in. The box had power again.

"Sam, can you unpause the movie?" his dad asked.

Sam looked at the box and saw another button with a symbol that looked like a triangle. He remembered that his dad told him that this button could unpause the movie.

"OK, dad. I can unpause the movie," Sam said.

He pressed the button and heard another click. The movie started to move again. It was unpaused.

"Yay, we did it! We fixed the movie!" Sam said.

He and his dad hugged and smiled. They went back to the couch and watched the rest of the movie. They enjoyed the movie and each other's company. Sam learned a new word and a new skill. He felt proud and happy. He still wanted to be like the man, but he also wanted to be like his dad. He thought his dad was very cool and strong too. He was his hero.

Ben nodded and said, "Yes, let's make soup. What should we put in it?" He looked around and saw some carrots, potatoes, and onions on the counter. He picked them up and put them in the pot. "There, now we have soup."

Anna smiled and said, "Good job, Ben. But we need to add some water and salt and pepper. And we need to turn on the stove to make it hot." She filled a cup with water and poured it in the pot. Then she sprinkled some salt and pepper from the shakers. She reached for the knob on the stove, but Ben stopped her.

"No, Anna, don't touch that. It's dangerous. Mommy said we can't touch the stove. It can burn us." He pulled her hand away and said, "We can pretend it's hot. Let's put the lid on the pot and lock it. Then the soup will cook by itself."

Anna agreed and said, "Okay, Ben, let's lock the pot. But how do we do that?" She looked at the lid and saw a handle on top. She pushed it down and heard a click. "There, I locked it. Now the soup is cooking."

They clapped their hands and said, "Yay, we made soup. Let's wait for a while and then we can eat it." They sat on the floor and played with some toys.

But after a few minutes, they heard a loud noise from the pot. It was bubbling and hissing and shaking. The lid was moving up and down and steam was coming out. Anna and Ben were frightened. They didn't know what was happening. They thought the pot was going to explode.

They ran to the door and shouted, "Mommy, Mommy, help us. The pot is angry. It's making noise and steam. We locked it and now we can't open it. Please come and save us."

Mommy heard their cries and came to the kitchen. She saw the pot and realized what had happened. She turned off the stove and used a cloth to grab the handle of the lid. She twisted it and opened the pot. The steam escaped and the bubbling stopped. She looked inside and saw the soup. It was overcooked and mushy.

She sighed and said, "Oh, Anna and Ben, what have you done? You locked the pot and turned on the stove. You could have started a fire or burned yourselves. You should never play with the stove or the pots. They are not toys. They are for cooking. And you should never lock the pot. It can build up pressure and explode. You were very lucky nothing bad happened."

Anna and Ben felt sorry and scared. They said, "We're sorry, Mommy. We didn't know. We wanted to make soup. We were pretending to be chefs. We won't do it again. Please don't be mad at us."

Mommy hugged them and said, "I'm not mad at you. I'm glad you're safe. But you have to be careful and listen to me. The kitchen can be dangerous. You can only play with the pots and pans when I'm with you. And you can only cook with me when I say so. Do you understand?"

Anna and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, Mommy, we understand. We love you. Thank you for saving us."

Mommy smiled and said, "I love you too. Now let's clean up this mess and make some real soup. How about that?"

Anna and Ben cheered and said, "Yes, Mommy, let's make some real soup. We want to help you. We want to be good chefs."

Mommy laughed and said, "Okay, let's do that. But first, let's unlock the pot and throw away this soup. It's not good to eat. It's too salty and too soft."

They unlocked the pot and dumped the soup in the trash. Then they washed the pot and the vegetables. They cut them and put them in a new pot with water and spices. They turned on the stove and watched the soup simmer. They didn't lock the pot this time. They learned their lesson. They were happy and hungry. They couldn't wait to eat their soup. They hoped it would be delicious.

"It means you give up and say I'm the best," Tim explained.

"But I don't want to do that, I have your flag," Sam said.

"Well, you have to, or I'll shoot you for real," Tim said.

Sam looked at Tim's stick and felt scared. He didn't want to get hurt. He looked at the flag and felt happy. He didn't want to give it back. He didn't know what to do.

"It's okay, Sam, you're a good soldier too," Tim said.

"Yes, I do!" Lily said, pointing to a pile of rocks. "Let's go there and dig for gold!"

They steered their ship towards the rocks and jumped out. They took their shovels and started to dig. They hoped they would find something shiny and valuable.

"Look, look!" Lily cried. "I found something!"

She held up a shiny coin. It was a chocolate coin wrapped in gold foil. Their mom had hidden it there for them to find.

"Wow, you did it!" Ben said. "You found treasure! You succeed!"

They hugged and cheered. They were very happy. They decided to share the coin and eat it together. They thanked their mom for the surprise. Then they went back to their ship and sailed to another adventure.

Lila and Tom were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big building with a wheel that turned and made noise. They wanted to know what it was, so they walked closer.

A man came out of the building and smiled at them. He was wearing a hat and a coat that were dusty. He said, "Hello, I am Sam. I work in the mill. This is where we make flour from wheat. Do you want to see?"

Lila and Tom nodded and followed Sam inside. He showed them how the wheat was stored in big bags, how the wheel was powered by water, and how the machines ground the wheat into fine powder. He gave them each a handful of flour to feel and smell.

Lila and Tom were amazed by the mill. They thanked Sam for showing them around. Sam said, "You are welcome. I am happy to introduce you to the mill. It is a humble place, but it is important. Without flour, we could not have bread, cakes, or cookies."

Lila and Tom agreed that flour was very good. They said goodbye to Sam and went back to the park. They decided to make a pretend mill with sticks and stones. They also pretended to bake bread and cookies with the flour. They had a lot of fun and learned something new.

Tom and Lily were on a big boat with their mom and dad. They liked to look at the water and the birds and the other boats. Sometimes they saw fish jumping out of the water.

"Look, Lily, there is a big fish!" Tom said, pointing at a gray shape in the water.

"Wow, it is so big! What is it?" Lily asked.

"It is a whale, Lily. A whale is a very big fish that can make loud noises and spray water from its head," Mom explained.

"Can we say hello to the whale, Mom?" Tom asked.

"Maybe, if we are lucky and quiet. The whale might come closer to our boat and pass by us," Mom said.

They waited and watched the whale. The whale swam slowly and came near their boat. They saw its big eye and its bald head. The whale made a loud noise and sprayed water from its head.

"Hello, whale!" Tom and Lily shouted.

The whale seemed to hear them and made another noise. Then it waved its tail and swam away.

"Bye, whale! Thank you for saying hello!" Tom and Lily said.

They waved at the whale until they could not see it anymore. Then they looked at the land. They saw many houses and boats and people.

"Where are we, Dad?" Tom asked.

"We are at the harbor, Tom. The harbor is a place where boats can stop and people can get on and off. We are going to get off our boat and visit our grandma and grandpa. They live near the harbor," Dad said.

"Yay, I love grandma and grandpa! Can we play with them and their dog?" Lily asked.

"Of course, Lily. They are waiting for us and they are very happy to see us. Come on, let's get our bags and go to the harbor," Dad said.

Tom and Lily were very excited. They got their bags and followed their mom and dad. They got off the big boat and walked to the harbor. They saw their grandma and grandpa waving at them. They ran to hug them and their dog. They were very happy to be at the harbor.

One day, Lily wanted to have a picnic in the backyard. She asked her mom if she could. Her mom said yes, but she had to clean her room first. Lily did not like to clean her room. She thought it was hard and boring.

She went to her room and looked at her toys. She had many toys, but she did not want to put them away. She had an idea. She called Spot and asked him to help her. She said, "Spot, can you please put my toys in the basket? It is easy for you. You have a big mouth and strong teeth. I will give you a treat if you do."

Spot liked treats. He nodded and wagged his tail. He picked up the toys with his mouth and put them in the basket. He did it very fast. Lily was happy. She said, "Good boy, Spot! You are very smart and helpful. Here is your treat. Thank you for helping me."

Lily and Spot went to the backyard. They had a picnic with sandwiches, cookies and juice. They shared their food and had fun. Lily's mom came and saw them. She smiled and said, "You did a good job, Lily. And you too, Spot. You are a good team. I'm proud of you." Lily and Spot hugged her and said, "We love you, mom." They had a happy day.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the park. They had a ball, a bike and a kite. They had fun throwing the ball, riding the bike and flying the kite. They were happy and hungry.

Their mom called them from the house. "Boys, come and eat! I made steak and salad for you!" She had a big smile and a big plate. The boys ran to the house. They loved steak. It was their favorite food.

They sat at the table and waited for their mom to cut the steak. Tim was older and bigger than Sam. He wanted the biggest piece of steak. He pointed at the plate and said, "I want that one! It is mighty and juicy!"

Sam was younger and smaller than Tim. He wanted the same piece of steak. He pointed at the plate and said, "No, I want that one! It is mighty and yummy!"

The boys started to shout at each other. "It is mine!" "No, it is mine!" "Give it to me!" "No, give it to me!" They pulled and pushed the plate. The plate fell on the floor. The steak and the salad spilled everywhere. The boys were sad and sorry.

Their mom came back to the kitchen. She saw the mess and the boys. She was angry and disappointed. She said, "Boys, what have you done? You wasted the food and made a mess! You should not shout and fight over the steak. You should share and be nice to each other. Now you have to clean up and say sorry."

The boys felt ashamed and guilty. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We were greedy and rude. We will clean up and share the steak. We love you, mom." They hugged their mom and each other. They learned a lesson and had a smaller steak. They were still happy and hungry.

Her mom smiled and said, "You have to open it and see, Lily. It is a surprise."

Lily tore the paper and saw a big box. She opened the box and saw something furry and brown. It was a teddy bear! But not a normal teddy bear. It was a giant teddy bear, bigger than Lily. Lily gasped and hugged the teddy bear. She loved it.

But then she heard a growl. She looked up and saw a real bear standing in the door. It was angry and hungry. It saw Lily and the teddy bear and thought they were food. It roared and ran towards them.

Lily was very scared. She and the teddy bear trembled. She screamed, "Mom, help!"

Her mom heard her and grabbed a broom. She ran to the bear and hit it on the nose. The bear was hurt and scared. It ran away and left them alone.

Lily was very thankful. She hugged her mom and said, "Thank you, mom. You are brave and strong."

Her mom hugged her back and said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are sweet and smart. And you have a new friend. What will you name him?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "I will name him Bear. He is my huge gift and my huge friend."

Tom and Lily were friends. They liked to play with cars and dolls. One day, they saw a big red bike in the park. It had a shiny buckle on the seat. Tom and Lily wanted to ride the bike.

They made a plan. Tom said, "I will ask the boy who owns the bike if we can have a turn. You wait here." Lily nodded. Tom ran to the boy and said, "Can we ride your bike, please?" The boy said, "No, it is mine. Go away." Tom felt sad and angry.

He went back to Lily and said, "The boy is mean. He won't let us ride his bike." Lily said, "That's not fair. Let's try again." They made a new plan. Lily said, "I will pretend to be hurt and cry. You go and get the bike when the boy comes to help me." Tom nodded. Lily lay down on the grass and started to cry.

The boy heard Lily and ran to her. He said, "What's wrong? Are you hurt?" Lily said, "Yes, I fell and scraped my knee. It hurts a lot." The boy said, "I'm sorry. Do you want a band-aid?" Lily said, "Yes, please." The boy said, "Wait here. I'll get one from my backpack." He left his bike and went to his backpack.

Tom saw his chance. He ran to the bike and grabbed it. He said, "Ha ha, we tricked you. Now we have your bike." He got on the bike and tried to ride away. But he forgot to buckle the seat. The seat slid off and Tom fell to the ground. The bike rolled away and hit a tree.

The boy saw what happened and laughed. He said, "That's what you get for being sneaky. You don't know how to ride a bike. You need a buckle to keep the seat on." He ran to his bike and picked it up. He said, "This is my bike. You can't have it." He buckled the seat and rode away.

Tom and Lily felt sorry and jealous. They wished they had a bike like the boy. They said, "Maybe we should not have lied. Maybe we should have asked nicely. Maybe we should have been his friend." They got up and walked away. They decided to play with their cars and dolls instead.

One day, they saw a new car in their toy box. It was big and red and had a hairy thing on top. Tim and Lily wondered what it was. They decided to try it out. They pushed the car to the gear and made it touch the teeth. But nothing happened. The car did not move the gear.

Tim and Lily tried harder. They pushed the car with both hands. They pushed the car with their feet. They pushed the car with their heads. But the car still did not move the gear. The car was too heavy and the hairy thing was too soft.

Tim and Lily felt sad. They wanted to make the gear move. They looked at their other cars. They saw a small and yellow car that had a hard thing on top. They thought maybe this car could move the gear. They pushed the small car to the gear and made it touch the teeth. And it worked! The car moved the gear and the gear made a funny noise.

Tim and Lily were happy. They laughed and clapped. They took turns pushing the small car and the gear. They forgot about the big and red car with the hairy thing. They had fun with their toy cars and the gear.

One day, a little boy named Tom wanted to go to a big event with his mom and dad. The event was at a park with many people, games, and balloons. Tom was very excited and ran to get his shoes.

But Tom did not tie his shoes well. He was in a hurry and did not listen to his mom, who told him to make a knot. He just made a loop and hoped it would stay.

When they got to the park, Tom saw a big slide. He wanted to try it and ran to the line. He waited for his turn and climbed to the top. He smiled and waved to his mom and dad.

But when he slid down, his shoe loop came undone. His foot slipped out of his shoe and he lost his balance. He bumped into another kid and they both fell off the slide. They landed on the grass, which was soft, but they still got hurt.

Tom and the other kid cried and their moms and dads came to help them. They had scratches and bruises and felt very sorry. Tom's mom gave him a hug and a band-aid. She said, "Tom, you should have tied your shoes well. Then you would not have slipped and hurt yourself and the other kid. Next time, please listen to me and do what I say. It is for your own good."

Tom nodded and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, other kid. I learned my lesson. I will tie my shoes well from now on. And I will listen to you and do what you say. I don't want to slip and hurt anyone again."

The other kid forgave Tom and they became friends. They played together at the park and had fun. Tom was careful and did not slip again. He enjoyed the event and thanked his mom and dad for taking him. He also thanked the soft grass for breaking his fall. He was happy and learned a moral value.

Lila and Ben were twins who liked to explore the forest near their home. They always took a big bag with them to fill with things they found. One day, they saw a big hole in the ground, covered with leaves and sticks.

"Look, Ben, what is this?" Lila asked, pointing at the hole.

"I don't know, Lila, maybe it's a secret cave," Ben said, curious.

They moved the leaves and sticks and peeked inside. It was dark and deep, and they heard a strange noise.

"Hello, who is there?" a voice said from the hole.

Lila and Ben were scared and jumped back.

"Who are you?" Ben asked, bravely.

"I am Toto, the original turtle of the forest. I live in this hole for a long time. Who are you?" the voice said.

Lila and Ben were surprised and excited. They had never seen a turtle before, let alone a talking one.

"We are Lila and Ben, we are twins. We like to explore the forest and fill our bag with things. Can we see you, Toto?" Lila asked, politely.

"Sure, you can see me, but you have to be careful. This hole is my home, and I don't like it when people touch my things," Toto said.

He slowly came out of the hole, and Lila and Ben saw his big shell and his small head. He was green and brown, and had a friendly smile.

"Wow, you are amazing, Toto. You are the original turtle of the forest. How old are you?" Ben asked, amazed.

"I am very old, I don't remember how old. I have seen many things in the forest, and I have many stories to tell. Do you want to hear some?" Toto asked.

"Yes, please, Toto. We love stories. Can we sit with you and listen?" Lila asked, eagerly.

"Of course, you can. But first, you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you will not tell anyone else about me. I like to be alone, and I don't want people to bother me. Can you do that?" Toto asked.

Lila and Ben nodded and crossed their hearts.

"We promise, Toto. We will not tell anyone. You are our secret friend," they said.

Toto smiled and nodded.

"Good, then come and sit with me. I will tell you some stories about the forest and the animals and the stars. And maybe, if you are nice, I will let you fill your bag with some of my things," he said.

Lila and Ben were happy and curious. They sat with Toto and listened to his stories. They learned a lot about the forest and the original turtle. They filled their bag with some of his things, like shiny stones and colorful feathers and soft moss. They thanked him and said goodbye. They promised to come back and visit him again. They ran back to their home, with their bag full and their hearts full. They had a new friend in the forest, and they felt very lucky.

One day, Sara went to the park with her mom and dad. She saw a big slide and wanted to try it. She ran to the slide and climbed up the ladder. She looked down and saw how high and long the slide was. She felt scared, but she wanted to be brave. She thought, "If I spin, I will not be scared." She spun around and around on top of the slide.

But spinning on the slide was not a good idea. Sara lost her balance and fell off the slide. She landed on the ground and hurt her knee. She cried and cried. Her mom and dad ran to her and hugged her. They checked her knee and saw that it was bleeding. They took her to the nurse and got a band-aid. The nurse told Sara that she should not spin on the slide. She said, "Spinning is fun, but you have to be careful where you spin. Some places are not safe for spinning."

Sara learned her lesson. She said sorry to her mom and dad and thanked the nurse. She looked at her blue dress and saw that it was dirty and torn. She felt sad, but she knew that it was her fault. She said, "I will not spin on the slide again. I will spin in safe places only."

The next day, Sara's mom washed her blue dress and hung it to dry. Sara saw her dress and smiled. It was still her favorite dress. She said, "Mom, can I wear my blue dress tomorrow?" Her mom said, "Yes, you can. But only if you promise to be careful when you spin." Sara nodded and hugged her mom. She said, "I promise, mom. I love you and I love my blue dress."

Zoe took the pastels and started to draw on the wall. She made a big mess and did not care. She saw the pink pastel under the books and grabbed it. She said, "This is the best color. I want it."

Mia saw what Zoe did and got very angry. She ran to Zoe and tried to take back her pink pastel. Zoe did not want to yield and pulled hard. The pastel broke in half and fell to the floor. Mia and Zoe both cried.

The teacher came and saw the broken pastel and the wall. She was very upset and scolded Mia and Zoe. She said, "You both did wrong. Mia, you should not be selfish and hide your things. Zoe, you should not be nosy and take what is not yours. And you both should not draw on the wall. That is naughty. You have to clean it up and say sorry to each other."

Mia and Zoe felt ashamed and sorry. They cleaned the wall and apologized to each other. They learned that being selfish and nosy can lead to trouble and sadness. They decided to be more kind and respectful to each other and to their things. They also learned to love all the colors of the pastels, not just the pink one.

Lila and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park. They have a ball and a bat. They take turns to strike the ball with the bat. They run and laugh.

One day, they see a big pond in the park. They have never seen it before. They go near the pond. They see something in the water. It is green and long. It has many teeth. It is a crocodile!

The crocodile sees them too. It is hungry. It jumps out of the water. It opens its mouth. It wants to eat them. Lila and Ben are scared. They scream.

"Help! Help! A crocodile!" they shout.

A man hears them. He is a park ranger. He has a stick. He runs to the pond. He sees the crocodile. He hits the crocodile with the stick. The crocodile is hurt. It goes back to the water. It swims away.

The man talks to Lila and Ben. He is kind.

"Are you okay, kids?" he asks.

"Yes, thank you, mister," they say.

"That was a bad crocodile. You should not go near the pond. It is dangerous. The pond is for the crocodiles, not for the kids. They are not healthy for you," he says.

"We are sorry, mister. We did not know. We will not go near the pond again. We will play with our ball and bat. They are healthy for us," they say.

The man smiles. He gives them a hug. He takes them back to their mom. She is happy to see them. She thanks the man. She gives them a kiss.

Lila and Ben are happy too. They learned a lesson. They will not play with crocodiles. They will play with their ball and bat. They are safe and healthy.

Lily and Ben were twins. They liked to play with their toys, but sometimes they wanted the same toy. One day, they saw a big red truck in the toy store. They both wanted it very much.

"Mom, can we have the truck?" they asked.

"Sorry, my loves, but we only have enough money for one toy today. You have to share or choose something else," Mom said.

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They did not want to share or choose something else. They both wanted the truck.

"I saw it first!" Lily said.

"No, I did!" Ben said.

They started to fight and pull the truck. Mom was sad. She did not like to see them fight.

"Lily, Ben, stop it! You are being very rude and selfish. If you can't play nicely, you can't have the truck at all. Let's go home," Mom said.

Lily and Ben did not listen. They ignored Mom and kept fighting. They did not see the other children in the toy store. They did not see how envious they were of the truck. They did not see how time was passing.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was the store owner. He was angry.

"Hey, you two! What are you doing? You are breaking the truck! Give it to me right now!" he shouted.

Lily and Ben let go of the truck. They were scared. They looked at Mom. She was very disappointed.

"I'm sorry, sir. They are usually not like this. They just really wanted the truck," Mom said.

"Well, they can't have it now. It's broken. And you have to pay for it. It was very expensive," the store owner said.

Lily and Ben felt very bad. They had wasted their money and their chance to have the truck. They had made Mom and the store owner unhappy. They had been very silly and greedy.

They hugged Mom and said they were sorry. They said they did not want the truck anymore. They said they would share and choose something else.

Mom smiled and hugged them back. She said she forgave them. She said they could still have one toy, but a cheaper one. She said they had to learn from their mistake and be more kind and grateful.

Lily and Ben nodded. They said they would. They looked around the toy store. They saw many other toys that they liked. They saw a doll and a car. They decided to share them. They were happy. They thanked Mom and the store owner. They left the toy store. They did not fight anymore. They played nicely. They did not ignore Mom or time or the other children. They did not feel envious of the truck. They felt lucky and loved.

She waited for Ben to answer, but she heard nothing. She started to feel scared. She called Ben again and again, but he did not reply. She wondered if he had left the park or got lost or hurt.

"Hello, little girl," he said. "Are you looking for someone?"

"Yes, I am looking for my friend Ben," Lily said. "He was playing hide and seek with me, but I can't find him. Have you seen him?"

The man nodded. "Yes, I have. He is in my bag. He is very good at hiding. Do you want to see him?"

Lily felt a chill in her heart. She remembered that her mom had told her not to talk to strangers or go with them. She tried to run away, but the man was faster. He grabbed her and put her in his bag too. He closed the bag and walked away.

Lily and Ben were in the dark. They were scared and sad. They wished they had not played hide and seek. They wished they had stayed in the shade. They wished they had listened to their mom. They wished they could call for help, but it was too late. The man had taken them away.

She learned that when the earth spun, it made day and night. She learned that when the sun was on the other side of the earth, it was night, and when the sun was on the same side of the earth, it was day. Lily started to dance and twirl around the blanket. She felt so happy and free. Her mom joined in and they danced together. "This is so much fun," Lily said. "I love dancing with you, Mom." They danced until the sun started to go down and it was time to go home. Lily felt so happy and comfortable as they walked back to their car.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly lady named Grandma. She lived in a tall building with many floors. To go up and down, she used the elevator. It was a small room that moved up and down like magic!

One day, Grandma went to the park with her grandson, Timmy. They played on the swings and the slide. Timmy loved sliding down the slide, but Grandma was too scared to try. She said, "Maybe next time."

As they were leaving the park, they saw a big sign that said, "Slide Festival this weekend!" Timmy was so excited and begged Grandma to take him. She smiled and said, "I have an idea. Let's take the elevator to the top of the building and slide down the stairs like a big slide!" 

Timmy was thrilled and they rode the elevator all the way up to the top. When they got out, they saw that the stairs were very steep and long. Grandma was scared, but Timmy held her hand and they slid down the stairs together, laughing and having fun. From that day on, Grandma was never afraid to slide again!

She even wore it to the dark forest and played with her friends. From that day on, the princess knew that if something didn't fit, there was always a way to make it better.

Once upon a time, there was a leopard who lived in the jungle. The leopard had a thick coat of fur that kept him warm. He loved to run and play in the jungle with his friends.

One day, the leopard found a fruit that was starting to rot. He was very hungry and wanted to eat it, but his friend, the monkey, told him not to eat it because it was bad for him. The leopard didn't listen and ate the fruit anyway.

Soon after, the leopard started to feel sick. His tummy hurt and he couldn't run and play anymore. He realized that his friend was right and he shouldn't have eaten the rotting fruit. The leopard felt sad and wished he had listened to his friend. From that day on, the leopard always listened to his friends and never ate anything that was starting to rot again.

Lily was curious about what was inside the box, so she decided to pull it open. Inside the box, she found a beautiful necklace. She was so happy and put it on right away.

Later that day, Lily's friend came over and saw the necklace. She wanted to have it too. Lily thought for a moment and then said, "I found it, so it's mine. But I can share it with you." Her friend was happy and they both wore the necklace together.

The moral of the story is that when we find something, we should share it with others. It's always better to share and make others happy too.

Lily said, "Oh no, how will we get past this big rock?"

Max went to the side of the rock and pushed it with all his might. The rock moved a little, but not enough for them to pass. Then, Max had another idea. Max smiled and said, "That's because we are a great team. We are dependable friends who can overcome any obstacle together."

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, I don't want my toys to get wet either."

"Wow, they are so pretty!" Lily said, admiring the roses.

Suddenly, they felt a cold splash on their backs. They turned around and saw the monkey, holding a water gun and smiling.

"Hey, monkey, that's not nice!" Lily said, feeling wet and cold.

"Ha ha, monkey is smart!" the monkey said, spraying them again.

Lily and Ben were surprised and angry. They grabbed their water guns and chased the monkey. The monkey ran and jumped and sprayed them back. They had a big water fight.

The monkey was having fun, but he was also competitive. He wanted to win. He sprayed Lily and Ben so much that they were soaked. They could not see or breathe well.

"Stop, monkey, stop!" Lily and Ben cried, dropping their water guns.

The monkey stopped and looked at them. He saw that they were not happy. He felt sorry. He dropped his water gun too.

"Sorry, Lily, sorry, Ben," the monkey said, coming closer to them.

"It's okay, monkey, we forgive you," Lily and Ben said, hugging the monkey.

"But next time, ask us before you play with our water guns," Lily said.

"Okay, next time, monkey ask," the monkey said, nodding.

They all smiled and went inside to dry off and have some bananas and nuts. They were still friends.

Foreshadowing or setup and payoff: The story uses foreshadowing when it says that Ben and Mia were almost ready to put the last block on top, implying that something might happen to stop them. So the mouse started to rub the thief's fur. The thief tried to get away, but he couldn't. He was so sore from the rubbing that he finally gave up and ran away.

The mouse had won! The thief never came back and the mouse kept the hat and the rubies safe. The mouse was very happy and proud that he had defeated the thief. The mouse was so happy that he danced around the wide field until he was too tired to dance anymore!

He tried and tried, but he just couldn't move. He tried to make a noise, but he only managed a soft crook. He was so scared.

Just then, a big white rabbit hopped over. He asked the frog what was wrong. The frog couldn't answer him, so he just shrugged his shoulder. The rabbit understood. He jumped into the water and picked up the frog. He then carried him to a safe spot in a nearby bush. 

The rabbit waved him goodbye and hopped away. The frog was so happy that his new friend had helped him. He jumped around until he felt better and went back to swimming. 

He smiled and thanked the white rabbit as he hopped away.

Once upon a time there was a little duck. His feathers were bright and golden. But one day, the duck became helpless. He was too big for his pond!

The duck was very sad. Then he had an idea. He took some oil from the pool and rubbed it onto his feathers. He did this every day for many days.

Suddenly, the duck started to shrink! He was so small he could fit into the pond! He splashed around happily.

The little duck stayed in the pond and always kept a bottle of oil with him. This way, he could always stay nice and small. The end.

She opened the yellow door, and inside she could see an old man. He was standing in the middle of the room and he was yelling very loudly! Jane was so scared! She wanted to run away, but she couldn't.

Suddenly the old man stopped yelling, and he looked right at Jane. He smiled and said, "Hello Jane! I'm so glad you're here. Let me show you something I found in the garden this morning." He turned around and showed Jane a round rock.

It was smooth and black, and it had a graceful pattern on it. Jane was so excited to discover this beautiful rock. She thanked the old man for showing it to her and then went on her way, taking the rock with her.

From that day on, Jane and the old man became good friends, and she always looked forward to her daily walks around her house.

So the swan ate the berry, and then flew away. But the swan soon felt sick. He landed in a nearby bush, feeling sicker and sicker as the minutes went by.

Suddenly a small, furry animal came to him.

"What happened to you, my friend?" said the animal.

The swan thanked the animal for the advice, and vowed never to eat something he did not know.

The moral of this story is: never taste something you do not know.

Her mom came to her room. She had a bowl of soup. "Lily, you need to eat some soup," she said. "Soup will make you feel better. It is warm and yummy."

Lily shook her head. She did not want soup. She wanted candy. "No, mom, I want candy," she said. "Candy is sweet and fun."

Her mom frowned. She knew candy was not good for Lily. "Candy will not help you, Lily," she said. "Candy will make you feel worse. It is too much sugar. You need soup, not candy."

Lily pouted. She did not like soup. She thought soup was boring and difficult. She did not want to eat it. She wanted to eat candy. She said, "No, mom, no soup. I want candy. Please, mom, please."

Her mom sighed. She loved Lily, but she also wanted Lily to be healthy. She had an idea. She said, "How about this, Lily? If you eat some soup, I will give you a little candy. Just one piece. But you have to eat some soup first. Deal?"

Lily thought about it. She really wanted candy. But she also wanted her mom to be happy. And she wanted to feel better. She nodded. She said, "Okay, mom, deal. I will eat some soup. But only a little. And then I want candy."

Lily and her mom ate some soup together. Lily did not like it very much, but she ate it anyway. She knew it was good for her. And she knew her mom loved her. And she knew she would get a little candy. She felt a little better. She learned a lesson. She was happy.

The cat said, "Hello little mouse. You can't escape from me now." But just then, Timmy's mommy and daddy came into the kitchen and scared the cat away. They helped Timmy untangle his tail from the knot and gave him some cheese to eat. Timmy was so happy that he didn't have to be fearful anymore.

Timmy nodded his head and gave her a piece of candy. Lily was very happy and said, "Thank you, Timmy! You are my best friend."

Timmy smiled and said, "I like to share my candy with my friends." 

From that day on, Lily and Timmy shared their candy with each other and became even better friends. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little monkey who loved to eat fruit. He would swing from tree to tree and pick the sweetest fruits he could find. One day, he saw a big, fierce tiger walking towards him. The monkey knew he had to be careful because the tiger was very dangerous.

The monkey quickly climbed up a tall tree and watched as the tiger walked around, searching for him. The monkey became very scared and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, he remembered he had a bag of fruit with him. He took out a juicy mango and threw it towards the tiger.

The tiger stopped and sniffed the mango. It smelled so good that he forgot all about the monkey. He walked over to the mango and started to eat it. The monkey became very happy because he knew he was safe. From that day on, the monkey always carried a bag of fruit with him, just in case he met any fierce animals.

Once upon a time, there was a little mole who lived in a big hole. He loved to dig tunnels and play in the dirt. One day, he met a rabbit who was hopping fast through the forest.

"I can't play now. I have to supply carrots to my family," replied the rabbit.

"What does supply mean?" asked the mole.

"It means to bring something to someone who needs it," explained the rabbit.

"Oh, I see. Can I help you supply carrots?" asked the mole.

"Sure, but you have to be fast like me," said the rabbit.

So, the mole and the rabbit worked together to supply carrots to the rabbit's family. The mole dug a tunnel to the carrot field, and the rabbit hopped fast to pick the carrots. They had so much fun working together that they became good friends.

"I am Anna, the princess. Who are you?" the girl answered.

"I am Tom, the bird. Why are you sad?" Tom asked.

"I am sad because I have to stay in the palace. I cannot go out and play. I have to learn and obey. I have no friends and no fun." Anna said.

"Fly with you? How can I do that? I have no wings." Anna said.

The moral of the story is: friendship can make you happy and free, and you can always find new ways to explore and enjoy the world.

Lily was happy. She thanked the clown and hugged her balloon. She ran back to her mom and dad, who were sitting on a bench. She showed them her balloon and said, "Look, mom and dad. I got a balloon from the clown. It's a dog. Isn't it cute?"

Mom and dad looked at the balloon and frowned. They saw something on the balloon that Lily didn't see. It was a pin. The clown had put a pin on the balloon. He was not nice and funny. He was mean and cruel. He wanted to make the kids cry.

Before Lily could say anything, the balloon popped. It made a loud noise and scared Lily. She dropped the balloon and started to cry. She felt sad and hurt. She didn't understand why the clown did that. She wanted her balloon back.

Mom and dad hugged Lily and tried to comfort her. They said, "It's okay, Lily. Don't cry. The clown was a bad man. He did a bad thing. We're sorry. We love you. We'll get you another balloon. A better one. Come on, let's go home."

Lily stopped crying and nodded. She held mom and dad's hands and walked with them. She looked back at the park and saw the clown. He was laughing and making more balloons. He seemed happy and proud. Lily felt angry and scared. She hated the clown. She wished he would go away. She never wanted to see him again.

"Dad, can you lift me up?" he asked.

"Sure, son," dad said and picked him up.

Tom was happy. He felt the elephant's trunk on his hand. It was rough and wet. The elephant made a loud noise.

"Hey, let go of my son!" dad shouted.

He tried to pull Tom back, but the elephant was too strong. It started to wander away with Tom, taking him to the other side of the fence.

"Help, help!" Tom cried.

Mom heard Tom's voice and ran to the fence. She saw the elephant holding Tom and walking away.

"Tom, Tom, where are you going?" she yelled.

She was scared and angry. She looked for a zookeeper to help them.

"Stop, stop, elephant!" she shouted.

The elephant heard mom's voice and stopped. It turned around and saw mom and dad. It realized that Tom was not one of its friends. It felt sorry and confused. It gently put Tom down and let go of his arm.

Tom was scared and sad. He ran to mom and dad and hugged them.

"I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I just wanted to say hello to the elephant," he said.

"It's OK, Tom, we're glad you're safe," mom said.

Tom nodded. He looked at the elephant and waved goodbye.

"Bye, elephant, I'm sorry too," he said.

The elephant waved its trunk and made a noise. It looked at Tom and seemed to say sorry too. It went back to its hay and left Tom and his parents alone.

Tom did not like what Sue said. He said, "No, I like my boat the way it is. It is not ugly. It is strong and fast and brave. And I like 'Sea Star'. It is a good name for a boat. You are not the boss of me. You can't tell me what to do with my boat."

Sue got angry. She said, "Yes, I am the boss of you. And I can tell you what to do with your boat. If you don't do what I say, I will break your boat. I will take your hammer and smash your mast. I will take your saw and cut your sail. I will take your nails and glue and throw them in the water."

Tom got scared. He did not want Sue to break his boat. He loved his boat. He said, "Please, don't break my boat. It is my favorite thing. I worked hard to fix it. Can't we be friends and share it?"

Sue thought for a moment. She said, "OK, fine. We can be friends and share it. But only if you let me paint it pink and put some flowers and ribbons on it and change the name to 'Princess Sue'."

Tom sighed. He did not want to do that. But he did not want to lose his boat. He said, "OK, fine. You can do that. But only if you let me fix it again when you are done."

Sue smiled. She said, "Deal. Let's go and get some paint and some flowers and some ribbons and some stickers. And then we can go sailing on 'Princess Sue'."

Tom did not like the way the boat looked. But he liked the way it sailed. And he liked having a friend. He hoped that Sue would let him fix it again soon. He missed his 'Sea Star'.

By sharing the toys, Amy gained more fun and more love from her friends. They all played together and had a great time. The moral of the story is that sharing can make everyone happy and bring more joy to our lives.

One day, a lawyer named Tom came to a small town. He arrived in a big car. Tom was new to the town and wanted to make friends. But Tom was a little rude. He did not know how to talk nicely to people.

Tom saw a girl named Lily. She was playing with her toy. Tom went to Lily and said, "Give me your toy!" Lily was sad and did not want to give her toy to Tom. She said, "No, it is mine!"

Tom felt bad. He knew he was rude and wanted to say sorry. So, he went to the store and bought a toy for Lily. He gave her the toy and said, "I am sorry. I was rude. Can we be friends?" Lily smiled and said, "Yes, we can be friends."

From that day, Tom and Lily played together. Tom learned to be nice to people. The town people liked Tom too. They were happy that the lawyer was not rude anymore.

Skelly asked, "Do you want to be my friend and play with me?" The dog wagged its tail and barked, "Yes, let's play together!"

Skelly and the dog played all day long. They ran, jumped, and laughed together. They became the best of friends. From that day on, Skelly was not alone in the hard, dark cave. He had his new friend, the dog, to keep him company. They lived happily ever after.

Tom was playing in the garden with his toy car. He liked to make it go fast and make loud noises. He saw a small beetle crawling on the grass. He wanted to catch it and look at it.

"Hello, beetle," he said. "You are very small and shiny. Can I hold you?"

The beetle did not mind. It was not afraid of Tom. It climbed on his finger and tickled him. Tom laughed and showed it to his mom.

"Look, mom, I found a beetle. It is my friend. Can I keep it?"

Mom smiled and shook her head. "No, Tom, you can't keep the beetle. It belongs to the garden. It needs to eat and drink and find other beetles. You can play with it for a little while, but then you have to let it go."

Tom nodded. He understood. He did not want to make the beetle sad. He played with it some more, then gently put it back on the grass.

"Bye, beetle," he said. "Thank you for playing with me. Maybe I will see you again."

The beetle waved its antennae and crawled away. Tom waved back and picked up his toy car. He was happy. He had made a new friend.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toys in the garden. Tom had a big hammer that he liked to bang on the ground. Lily had a soft doll that she liked to hug and dress. They were both very happy.

But then, Tom saw Lily's doll and wanted to play with it. He ran to Lily and grabbed the doll from her hands. Lily was very sad and angry. She shouted, "No, Tom! That is my doll! Give it back!"

Tom did not listen. He held the doll with one hand and the hammer with the other. He was about to hit the doll with the hammer, when he heard a loud voice.

"Stop, Tom! What are you doing?" It was their dad, who had come to see what was the noise. He saw Tom with the doll and the hammer, and Lily crying. He was not jolly at all. He was very cross.

He took the doll and the hammer from Tom and gave them back to Lily. He said, "Tom, you should not take things from Lily without asking. That is not nice. You should share your toys with your sister, and she will share hers with you. Do you understand?"

Tom nodded. He felt sorry for making Lily cry. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. Can I play with your doll, please?"

Lily did not like vegetables. She thought they were yucky and green and hard. She only wanted to eat cheese and bread and cake. Her mom was sad and angry. She wanted Lily to be healthy and strong.

One day, mom made a big salad for lunch. She put many vegetables in it: lettuce, tomato, carrot, cucumber, and corn. She also put some cheese and bread on the side. She called Lily to the table and said, "Lily, come and eat your lunch. It is good for you."

Lily came to the table and looked at the salad. She made a face and said, "No, I don't want to eat that. I only want cheese and bread and cake."

Mom said, "Lily, you have to eat some vegetables. They have vitamins and minerals that help you grow and learn. They are also tasty and crunchy. Why don't you try one and see?"

Lily shook her head and said, "No, I don't want to try. I know they are yucky and green and hard. I am not hungry."

Mom said, "Lily, you are being stubborn. You have to eat something or you will be hungry later. How about this? If you touch one vegetable with your tongue, you can have a piece of cake after lunch. Just touch it, you don't have to bite it."

Lily thought for a moment. She liked cake very much. She looked at the salad and saw a small piece of corn. She liked corn. It was yellow and sweet and soft. She decided to touch it with her tongue. She reached out her hand and picked up the corn. She brought it to her mouth and touched it with her tongue. It was not yucky. It was yummy. She liked it. She smiled and said, "Mom, I touched a vegetable. Can I have cake now?"

Mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can have cake now. But first, why don't you try another vegetable? Maybe you will like it too."

Lily nodded and said, "OK, mom. I will try another vegetable. Maybe I will like it too." She looked at the salad and saw a small piece of carrot. She picked it up and touched it with her tongue. It was not hard. It was crunchy. She liked it. She said, "Mom, I like carrot. It is crunchy."

Mom said, "I'm glad you like carrot. It is good for your eyes and your skin. Do you want to try another vegetable?"

Lily said, "Yes, mom. I want to try another vegetable. Maybe I will like it too." She looked at the salad and saw a small piece of tomato. She picked it up and touched it with her tongue. It was not green. It was red and juicy. She liked it. She said, "Mom, I like tomato. It is juicy."

Mom said, "I'm happy you like tomato. It is good for your heart and your blood. Do you want to try another vegetable?"

Lily said, "Yes, mom. I want to try another vegetable. Maybe I will like it too." She looked at the salad and saw a small piece of cucumber. She picked it up and touched it with her tongue. It was not hard. It was cool and fresh. She liked it. She said, "Mom, I like cucumber. It is cool and fresh."

Mom said, "I'm proud of you, Lily. You tried four vegetables and you liked them all. You are not stubborn anymore. You are brave and curious. You can have your cake now. But first, why don't you eat some salad? It will make you full and happy."

Lily said, "OK, mom. I will eat some salad. It will make me full and happy. And then I will have cake. Thank you, mom. I love you."

Mom said, "You're welcome, Lily. I love you too." She hugged Lily and gave her a kiss. They ate their lunch together and enjoyed their cake. Lily learned that vegetables were not yucky and green and hard. They were tasty and crunchy and juicy and fresh. She decided to try more vegetables in the future. She was not stubborn anymore. She was brave and curious. And she was healthy and strong.

But then she saw something shiny on the snow. It was a patch of ice. It looked like a mirror. Lily was curious. She wanted to see what was on the ice. She leaned over the edge of her sled and reached out her hand. She touched the ice. It was very cold and slippery. She felt a tingle in her fingers.

"Wow, this is icy!" she said out loud.

But then she lost her balance. She slid off her sled and onto the ice. She started to slide down the hill very fast. She was scared. She tried to stop, but she couldn't. She screamed for help.

Her mom heard her scream. She ran to the hill and saw Lily sliding down. She was worried. She grabbed another sled and followed Lily. She caught up with her and grabbed her hand. She pulled her onto her sled and hugged her.

"Lily, are you okay?" she asked.

Lily was shaking and crying. She was glad her mom was there. She hugged her back.

Her mom kissed her cheek and rubbed her back.

"It's okay, Lily. I'm here. You're safe. Next time, don't lean over the ice. It's dangerous. Just stay on your sled and have fun. Okay?" she said.

Lily nodded and smiled.

"Okay, mom. Thank you. I love you," she said.

Her mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. Now let's go home and have some hot chocolate. How does that sound?"

Lily nodded and said, "That sounds good, mom. Let's go."

They got off the hill and walked home, holding hands. Lily learned a lesson that day. She learned to be careful with the ice and to listen to her mom. She also learned that her mom loved her very much and would always help her. She was happy.
