Lila and Ben were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big basket of grapes on a bench. They were hungry and wanted some grapes.

"Can we have some grapes?" Lila asked the lady who was sitting on the bench.

"Sure, you can have some grapes. But be careful, they have seeds inside. You have to spit them out," the lady said.

"Thank you, lady. You are very nice," Ben said.

Lila and Ben took some grapes and started to eat them. They were sweet and juicy. They spat out the seeds on the grass.

"Yum, these grapes are good," Lila said.

"Yes, they are. But look, there is a bee. It wants some grapes too," Ben said.

They saw a yellow and black bee flying around the basket. It landed on a grape and tried to bite it.

"Ouch, the bee bit me!" the lady shouted. She jumped up and ran away.

Lila and Ben were scared. They dropped their grapes and ran away too.

They hid behind a tree and watched the bee. It was still biting the grapes.

"Bad bee. Go away. Leave the grapes alone," Lila said.

"Yes, go away. The grapes are for us and the lady," Ben said.

But the bee did not listen. It kept biting the grapes until it was full. Then it flew away.

Lila and Ben came out from behind the tree. They saw the basket of grapes. It was still half full.

"Maybe we can have some more grapes," Lila said.

"Maybe. But we have to be quick. The bee might come back," Ben said.

They ran to the basket and grabbed some more grapes. They ate them fast and spat out the seeds.

They were grateful for the grapes. They were grateful for the lady. They were not grateful for the bee.

"Yes, it is!" Ben says. "We are good designers!"

They are happy and proud of their tower. They want to show it to their mom and dad. They run to the kitchen to get them.

"Mom, dad, come and see our tower!" Lily and Ben say. "We made it with blocks!"

Mom and dad follow them to the living room. They see the cool tower and smile.

"Wow, what a cool tower!" Mom says. "You did a great job, Lily and Ben!"

"It is very impressive!" Dad says. "You are very creative and smart!"

Lily and Ben hug their mom and dad. They are glad they like their tower. They want to play with blocks again and design more cool things.

Sara likes to collect shells on the beach. She has a big bucket and a small shovel. She digs and digs and finds many shells. Some are big and some are small. Some are shiny and some are dull. Sara loves all the shells.

One day, Sara sees a very ugly shell. It is brown and bumpy and has holes. Sara does not like the ugly shell. She says, "Yuck! I don't want this shell. It is ugly and dirty. I want pretty shells." She throws the ugly shell away.

But then, a crab comes out of the sand. The crab is angry. He says, "Hey! That is my shell. You can't throw it away. It is my home. It is not ugly and dirty. It is cozy and warm. I like my shell."

Sara is surprised. She says, "Oh, I'm sorry. I didn't know it was your shell. I thought it was just a shell. I didn't mean to make you angry. You can have your shell back."

The crab is happy. He says, "Thank you. You are very nice. You can have some of my cream. It is sweet and yummy. I found it in a can. Do you like cream?"

Sara smiles. She says, "Yes, I like cream. Thank you. You are very nice too. Can we be friends?"

The crab nods. He says, "Yes, we can be friends. You can collect shells and I can collect cream. We can share and have fun."

Sara and the crab become friends. They collect shells and cream together. They learn that ugly and pretty are not the same for everyone. They learn that different things can be good and bad. They learn that being kind and sharing are the best.

Tim and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big furry dog. The dog is brown and has a long tail. The dog is happy and runs to them.

"Hi, dog!" Tim says. "Can we pet you?"

The dog wags his tail and licks Tim's face. Jen laughs and pets the dog too. The dog likes them. He barks and jumps.

But then a man comes. The man is angry. He has a leash and a badge. He is a dog catcher.

"Stop!" the man yells. "That dog is bad! He ran away from the jail!"

The man tries to catch the dog. But the dog is fast. He runs away from the man. The man chases the dog.

Tim and Jen are scared. They do not want the dog to go to jail. They want the dog to be free.

"Come on, dog!" Jen shouts. "We will help you!"

Tim and Jen run after the dog. They try to block the man. But the man is big. He pushes them away.

"Get out of my way, kids!" the man says. "That dog is mine!"

The man is close to the dog. He reaches for the leash. But then he trips. He falls on the ground. He drops the leash.

The dog sees the leash. He grabs it with his mouth. He runs to Tim and Jen. He gives them the leash.

"Good dog!" Tim says. "You are smart!"

The dog wags his tail. He is happy. He likes Tim and Jen.

Tim and Jen hold the leash. They look at the man. The man is angry. He gets up. He walks to them.

"Give me that leash, kids!" the man says. "That dog is going to jail!"

Tim and Jen shake their heads. They do not want to give the leash. They want to keep the dog.

"No!" Tim says. "He is our dog now!"

The man is mad. He tries to grab the leash. But then a woman comes. The woman is nice. She has a car and a sign. She is a vet.

"Stop!" the woman says. "That dog is not yours! He is mine!"

The woman shows the man a paper. The paper has a picture of the dog and a name. The name is Max.

"Max is my dog!" the woman says. "He escaped from my car when I was at the park. He is not bad. He is just scared. He is not going to jail. He is going home with me!"

The man looks at the paper. He sees the picture and the name. He sees the woman's sign and car. He knows he is wrong.

"Sorry, lady," the man says. "I did not know. I thought he was a stray."

The woman takes the leash from Tim and Jen. She pets Max. Max licks her face.

"Thank you, kids," the woman says. "You are very kind. You saved Max from the jail. Do you want to come with me and see where he lives?"

Tim and Jen nod. They want to see where Max lives. They want to be his friends.

"OK," the woman says. "Let's go!"

The woman, Max, Tim and Jen get in the car. They drive away from the park. They leave the man behind. The man is sad. He has no dog.

Red felt sad and worried. He didn't know what to do. Blue suggested they ask their other friends for help. They went to see Yellow and Green, who were happy to lend Red the money he needed. With their help, Red was able to own the fix and his engine was soon running smoothly again.

From that day on, Red was grateful to his friends and promised to always ask for help when he needed it.

"Stop it, bird!" he said. "You are mine. You have to do what I say."

The bird did not stop. It bit Tom's finger hard. Tom screamed and let go of the bird. The bird flew away, fast and free. It flew to the west, where the sun was setting. It sang a loud and happy song.

Tom cried and rubbed his finger. He felt pain and shame. He wished he had listened to Sue. He wished he had left the bird alone.

Sue came to Tom and hugged him. She felt sorry for him. She also felt sorry for the bird.

"Tom, I hope you learned a lesson," she said. "You should not slap or catch things that are not yours. You should be kind and gentle to all living things. They have feelings too, like you and me."

Tom nodded and hugged Sue back. He said he was sorry. He said he would be kind and gentle from now on. He said he hoped the bird was okay.

The bird was okay. It found a new tree and a new friend. It sang a pretty song every day. It never saw Tom or Sue again. But it remembered them. It remembered the slap and the cage. It also remembered the hug and the sorry. It hoped Tom and Sue were okay too. It hoped they were kind and gentle to all living things. It hoped they were happy.

Mom hugged Tim and wiped his tears. She smiled and said, "Don't worry, Tim. I know someone who can fix Bob. He is a robot doctor. He can make Bob walk, talk, and light up again. He can also teach you how to take care of Bob and not break him. Do you want to go see him?"

You should not touch things that are not yours. You should ask before you take something. You should be careful with things that are fragile. You should respect other people's feelings. Do you understand?"

Lily felt very sorry. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I did not know. I thought it was ugly and old. I wanted to throw it away. I wanted to weigh it. I did not mean to break it. I love you, mom. I love grandma, too. Can you forgive me?"

Mom said, "I love you, too, Lily. I forgive you. But you have to learn from your mistake. You have to be more responsible and respectful. You have to appreciate things that are not modern, but have history and meaning. You have to say sorry to grandma, too. She is watching over us from heaven. She loves you, too."

Lily nodded. She said, "I'm sorry, grandma. I will be a better girl. I will listen to mom. I will be more careful. I will be more grateful. I will love you more."

Mom smiled. She said, "That's good, Lily. I'm proud of you. Now, let's clean up this mess and find a way to remember grandma. Maybe we can make a collage with the pieces of the ashtray. What do you think?"

Lily liked the idea. She said, "Yes, mom. Let's do that. Let's make something beautiful and new with something old and broken. Let's make grandma happy."

Mom and Lily hugged. They felt closer and happier. They learned a lesson. They learned to value what they had and who they loved. They learned to say sorry and to forgive. They learned to be creative and to be kind. They learned to be a family.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and balls. One day, they find a big box in the park. They open the box and see many toys inside. They are very happy.

But then, a big boy comes. He is mean and angry. He says, "These are my toys. Go away or I will hit you." He makes a threat. Tom and Sam are scared. They do not want to fight.

Tom has an idea. He says, "OK, we will go. But first, can we tell you a joke?" The big boy is curious. He likes jokes. He says, "Fine. But make it quick."

Tom says, "What do you call a fish that wears a hat?" The big boy thinks. He does not know. He says, "I don't know. What?"

Tom says, "A head fish!" He and Sam laugh. They think it is funny. The big boy does not laugh. He thinks it is silly. He says, "That is a bad joke. It is not funny at all."

Tom says, "OK, OK. How about this one? What do you call a bird that can fly very fast?" The big boy says, "I don't know. What?"

Tom says, "A rare bird!" He and Sam laugh again. They think it is clever. The big boy does not laugh. He thinks it is stupid. He says, "That is a worse joke. It is not clever at all."

Tom says, "OK, OK. One more. What do you call a dog that can talk?" The big boy says, "I don't know. What?"

Tom says, "A joke!" He and Sam laugh very loud. They think it is the best joke. The big boy does not laugh. He thinks it is the worst joke. He says, "That is not a joke. That is a lie."

But then, he sees something. He sees a dog behind the box. The dog is big and brown. The dog says, "Woof! Woof! I am a joke!" The big boy is shocked. He thinks it is a miracle. He says, "Wow! A talking dog! That is rare!"

Tom and Sam smile. They say, "Surprise! The dog is our friend. He can make funny sounds. He helped us with the joke. We wanted to make you laugh. We did not want to fight."

The big boy feels silly. He says, "Oh. I see. You are very smart. And funny. And brave. I am sorry I was mean. Can we be friends?"

Tom and Sam say, "Yes, we can. Friends are good. And jokes are good. And toys are good. Can we share the toys?"

The big boy says, "Yes, we can. Sharing is good. And playing is good. And laughing is good. Come on, let's play."

One day, their mom said, "It is almost time for your birthday. You can decorate your room with balloons and stickers. But you have to do it together. No fighting, okay?"

"No, I want the red balloon. It is bigger and prettier," Tom said.

They pulled and tugged at the balloon. It popped with a loud bang. They both cried.

"What happened?" she asked.

"We wanted the same balloon. We fought over it. And it broke," Sara said.

"That is not good. You should not fight over things. You should share and be kind. Then you will have more fun and less trouble," Mom said.

She gave them a hug and a tissue. She helped them to decorate their room with the other balloons and stickers. They made it look nice and colorful.

Sara and Tom learned their lesson. They said sorry to each other. They decided to share and be kind. They had a happy birthday. They enjoyed their room and their toys and books. They did not fight anymore. They were good twins.

"Good night, Sara," her mom said. "Sleep tight and don't let the bedbugs bite."

"Good night, mom," Sara said. "I love you."

She saw her brother Tom. He was holding a big jar of cookies. He had a sneaky smile on his face. He took out a cookie and was about to eat it.

"Tom, what are you doing?" Sara asked. "You are not supposed to eat cookies before bed. You will get a tummy ache. And you will disturb mom and dad. They are sleeping."

Tom jumped and dropped the cookie. He looked guilty and scared. He knew he was in trouble.

"Sara, don't tell mom and dad," he begged. "Please, please, please. I was just hungry. And I love cookies. They are so yummy. Please, Sara, be nice."

Sara thought for a moment. She liked cookies too. But she also knew the rules. She decided to be a good sister and help Tom.

"OK, Tom, I won't tell mom and dad," she said. "But you have to put back the cookies and go to bed. And you have to brush your teeth again. And you have to promise me you won't do this again. Deal?"

"Deal," Tom said. "Thank you, Sara. You are the best sister ever."

They hugged and put back the cookies. They brushed their teeth and went back to their beds. They said good night to each other and fell asleep. They both had sweet dreams. And they didn't disturb anyone.

One day, Tom saw a big truck on the street. It was red and shiny, and it had a loud horn. Tom wanted to see the truck up close, so he ran after it. He whistled as he ran, hoping the driver would hear him and stop.

The driver did hear him, and he saw him in the mirror. He smiled and waved at Tom, and slowed down the truck. He opened the door and said, "Hello, little whistler. Do you want to see my truck?"

Tom nodded and climbed up the seat. He was very happy. The driver showed him the steering wheel, the pedals, the buttons, and the horn. He let Tom whistle into the radio and talk to other drivers. He even gave him a hat that said "Truck Driver" on it.

Tom felt very fit. He felt like he could drive the truck himself. He thanked the driver and gave him a hug. He put on his hat and whistled as he got down. He waved goodbye to the driver and ran back to his mom and dad. He told them all about his adventure, and they were very proud of him. He was Whistling Tom, the truck driver.

Tom and Lily liked to play chess with their dad. Chess was a game with black and white pieces that moved on a board with squares. Tom and Lily learned how to move the pieces from their dad, who was very good at chess.

One night, Tom and Lily could not sleep. They saw a light in the living room. They got out of bed and went to see what it was. They saw their dad playing chess with a strange man. The man had a long beard and a hat. He also had a big bag with him.

The man was not a normal man. He was a wizard. He came from a faraway land where magic was real. He was looking for a chess partner who could challenge him. He saw the light in Tom and Lily's house and knocked on the door. Their dad was surprised, but he was also curious. He invited the wizard in and agreed to play chess with him.

The wizard was very good at chess. He moved his pieces with a flick of his wand. His pieces also glowed with different colors. Red for the king, blue for the queen, green for the bishops, yellow for the knights, orange for the rooks, and purple for the pawns. The colors made the game more fun and easy to see.

Tom and Lily watched the game with wonder. They wanted to help their dad win. They whispered to each other and pointed at the board. They saw a move that their dad did not see. They told their dad to move his queen to a square where she could capture the wizard's king. Their dad listened to them and made the move. The wizard was shocked. He had lost the game.

The wizard smiled and clapped his hands. He praised Tom and Lily for being helpful and clever. He gave them each a glowing chess piece as a gift. He also gave their dad a book of chess puzzles and secrets. He thanked them for the game and said goodbye. He waved his wand and disappeared in a flash of light.

Tom and Lily were very happy. They hugged their dad and thanked him for playing chess with them. They went back to their bed and put their glowing chess pieces under their pillows. They fell asleep and dreamed of magic and chess.

"Wow, look at that!" Ben said. "It is so big and shiny!"

"I am scared," Anna said. "It is too loud and scary. Let's go inside."

They ran to the house and closed the door. They looked out the window and saw more lightning and rain. They heard another boom and saw a big tree fall down.

"Oh no, the tree!" Anna said. "It was so tall and green. Now it is broken and brown."

"Maybe we can find something to fix it," Ben said. He was brave and curious. He liked to find things and make things.

"How can we fix it?" Anna asked. She was sad and worried. She liked the tree and the animals that lived in it.

"Maybe we can find some glue or tape or string," Ben said. He looked around the house for something to use.

He found some glue in the drawer, some tape in the box, and some string in the closet. He took them outside and ran to the tree.

"Come on, Anna, help me!" he said. He tried to glue and tape and tie the tree back together.

Anna followed him and tried to help. She was still scared of the lightning, but she wanted to help the tree.

They worked hard and long, but the tree was too big and deep. They could not fix it.

They heard their mom call them from the house.

"Anna, Ben, come inside now! It is not safe to be outside in the storm!"

They left the glue and the tape and the string and ran to the house. They hugged their mom and told her what they tried to do.

"That was very kind and brave of you, but you can't fix a tree with glue and tape and string," she said. "The tree is too deep and strong. It will heal by itself in time. But you can find other ways to help the animals that lived in the tree. Maybe you can make them a new home or give them some food or water."

"Really?" Anna and Ben asked.

"Yes, really," their mom said. "Let's find out what they need and what we can do. But first, let's have some hot chocolate and cookies. You must be cold and hungry after being outside in the storm."

They smiled and nodded. They followed their mom to the kitchen and had some hot chocolate and cookies. So, Benny and Timmy clapped their paws loudly. The hunter heard the noise and thought it was a big animal. He got scared and ran away. Benny was happy and thanked Timmy for being such a good friend. From that day on, Benny and Timmy always clapped their paws together when they were scared.

When they arrived at the amusement park, Lily saw all the colorful balloons and decorations. She knew they were there to celebrate her birthday. She couldn't wait to go on the rides and play games with her family.

As the day went on, Lily had so much fun. She went on all the rides and won a prize at one of the games. At the end of the day, her parents brought out a big cake with candles on it. Lily blew out the candles and made a wish. She felt so happy and loved. Today was the best day ever!

Suddenly, she saw a flower that didn't look fit. It was drooping and sad. Lily asked her mommy, "Why is this flower not happy like the others?" Her mommy replied, "Maybe it needs some water and sunshine to bloom." 

Lily decided to help the flower. She gave it some water and put it near the window to get some sunshine. After a few days, the flower started to bloom beautifully. Lily was so proud of herself for helping the flower. She said, "Look mommy, the flower is fit now and it bloomed!"

Her mom gave her a big hug and said, "Don't worry, Lily. You are not boring. You are special in your own way. Just keep being yourself and you will find friends who love you for who you are." From that day on, Lily learned that it's okay to be different and that true friends will accept you for who you are.

When Sunshine woke up, he had the warmest, happiest feeling ever. And he thanked his friend the friendly dog for showing him the way to the shady tree where he could rest.

Mira and Tom liked to spend time at the beach. They liked to play in the sand, splash in the water, and look for shells. One day, they found a big shell that was closed. Tom said, "Maybe there is a pearl inside. Let's open it and see."

Mira said, "No, Tom. That is not a shell. That is an oyster. Oysters are alive. They have a soft body inside the shell. They need the shell to protect them. If we open it, we will hurt the oyster."

Tom said, "But I want to see the pearl. Pearls are shiny and pretty. Maybe we can keep it and make a necklace."

Mira said, "Tom, pearls are very rare. Not all oysters have pearls. And even if they do, they make the pearls because something hurts them. A grain of sand or a tiny bug gets inside the shell and the oyster covers it with a smooth layer. That is how a pearl grows. It takes a long time and a lot of work. The pearl is the oyster's treasure. We should not take it away."

Tom said, "Oh, I did not know that. I do not want to hurt the oyster or take its treasure. I want to be kind to the oyster. What can we do?"

Mira said, "We can put the oyster back in the water. Maybe it will find a friend or a family. Maybe it will make more pearls. We can say goodbye and thank you to the oyster for letting us see its beautiful shell."

Tom said, "OK, Mira. That sounds good. Let's do that."

They gently placed the oyster back in the water and watched it sink. They saw a flash of light as the sun hit the shell. They smiled and waved. They thought the oyster was very graceful and brave. They were happy to spend time at the beach and learn something new. They decided to look for more oysters and other creatures and respect their lives. They had a lot of fun and made a lot of memories.

Molly said, "I'm Molly. This is Spot. He is sick. Can you help him?"

Lily made a face. She did not think broccoli was good for her. She thought it was yucky and gross. She did not want to be strong and healthy. She wanted to be happy and sweet.

"Mama, please. I do not like broccoli. It makes me sad. Can I have something else?" she begged.

Mama sighed. She loved Lily very much, but she also wanted her to eat well. She had an idea.

"How about this, Lily? If you eat three bites of broccoli, I will permit you to have a small piece of cake. Just three bites. That is not too much. Do you think you can do that?" she offered.

Lily thought about it. She really wanted cake. Cake was soft and sweet and yummy. But she also really hated broccoli. Broccoli was hard and bitter and yucky. She looked at her plate. There were five pieces of broccoli. She only had to eat three. That meant she could leave two. Maybe that was not so bad.

Mama smiled and nodded. "Right. Three bites and then cake. I am proud of you, Lily. You are a brave and good girl."

Lily doubted that. But she did not say anything. She just enjoyed her cake and her Mama. And she was glad that Mama permitted her to have cake after eating broccoli. That was a good deal.

One day, a cat saw a mouse in the garden. The cat was hungry and wanted to catch the mouse. He ran after the mouse, but the mouse was fast and smart. The mouse ran under a bush, then behind a rock, then into a hole.

The cat was angry and tried to dig the hole with his paws. He said, "Come out, mouse, I want to eat you!"

But the mouse did not come out. He said, "No, cat, you are fierce and mean. I do not want to be your food!"

The cat and the mouse stayed like that for a long time. The cat could not reach the mouse, and the mouse could not pass the cat.

Then, a dog came to the garden. The dog saw the cat and the mouse. The dog was friendly and wanted to play. He barked, "Hello, cat and mouse, do you want to play with me?"

The cat and the mouse were scared of the dog. They said, "No, dog, you are big and loud. We do not want to play with you!"

The dog did not listen. He ran to the hole and sniffed it. He said, "What are you doing in there, mouse? Come out and play!"

The mouse was very afraid. He said, "Help, cat, help!"

The cat was surprised. He said, "Help you, mouse? Why should I help you?"

The mouse said, "Please, cat, we are both small and furry. The dog is our enemy. If you help me, I will give you some cheese."

The cat thought for a moment. He liked cheese. He said, "Okay, mouse, I will help you. But you have to be quick."

The cat and the mouse made a plan. The cat said to the dog, "Dog, you are silly and slow. I bet you cannot catch me!"

The dog said, "Yes, I can, cat. I am fast and strong. I will show you!"

The cat ran away from the hole. The dog ran after him. The mouse saw his chance. He passed the dog and ran to the fence. He found a small gap and squeezed through it. He was safe.

The cat also ran to the fence. He jumped over it. He was safe too.

The dog was confused. He said, "Where did they go? I wanted to play with them!"

The cat and the mouse looked at each other from the other side of the fence. The mouse said, "Thank you, cat, for helping me. Here is some cheese for you."

The cat said, "You are welcome, mouse, for helping me too. You are smart and brave. Maybe we can be friends."

The mouse said, "Maybe we can, cat. But only if you do not try to eat me again."

The cat said, "I promise, mouse, I will not try to eat you again. But only if you do not take my milk again."

The mouse said, "I promise, cat, I will not take your milk again. But only if you share it with me sometimes."

The cat said, "Okay, mouse, I will share it with you sometimes. But only if you share your cheese with me too."

The mouse said, "Okay, cat, I will share my cheese with you too. But only if you are nice to me."

The cat said, "Okay, mouse, I will be nice to you. But only if you are nice to me too."

The mouse said, "Okay, cat, I will be nice to you too."

And so, the cat and the mouse became friends. They passed the fence and went to the barn. They found some milk and some cheese. They ate and drank and played together. They were happy.

Tom was a king who liked to eat lemons. He thought lemons made him strong and smart. He ate lemons every day, even for breakfast. He did not care that lemons were sour and made his face funny.

One day, a girl named Sue came to visit the king. She brought him a cake with icing and sprinkles. She said, "Hello, King Tom. I made this cake for you. It is sweet and yummy. Do you want to try some?"

King Tom looked at the cake and said, "No, thank you. I only eat lemons. They improve my health and my mind. Cakes are bad for you. They make you fat and lazy."

Sue was sad. She said, "But lemons are too sour. They hurt your teeth and your tongue. Cakes are good for you. They make you happy and friendly. Please, try a bite of my cake. You might like it."

King Tom shook his head. He said, "No, no, no. I will not eat your cake. Go away and leave me alone with my lemons."

Sue was very sad. She left the cake on the table and went away. She thought, "King Tom is a silly and rude king. He does not know how to enjoy life. He does not have any friends. He only has lemons."

The next day, King Tom woke up with a toothache. He tried to eat a lemon, but it made him scream. He called for a doctor, but the doctor said, "You have too many cavities. You need to stop eating lemons and eat something else. Like this cake that Sue left for you. It has milk and eggs and flour and sugar. They are good for your teeth and your bones and your energy."

King Tom did not want to eat the cake. He said, "But I like lemons. They improve me. They make me a better king."

The doctor said, "No, they do not. They make you a worse king. They make you sour and lonely and unhappy. You need to eat something sweet and share it with others. That will improve you. That will make you a kind and generous and joyful king."

King Tom thought about what the doctor said. He looked at the cake and thought, "Maybe the doctor is right. Maybe I should try the cake. Maybe I will like it. Maybe Sue will come back and be my friend."

He took a bite of the cake and smiled. It was sweet and yummy. He felt a warm and fuzzy feeling in his heart. He said, "This cake is delicious. I want more. And I want to share it with Sue and everyone else. I want to be a good king. I want to improve."

He called for Sue and said, "Sue, I am sorry. I was wrong. Your cake is wonderful. Thank you for making it for me. Will you please come and eat some with me? And will you please be my friend?"

Sue was happy. She said, "Of course, King Tom. I am glad you like my cake. And I am glad you want to be my friend. You are a good king. You have improved."

They ate the cake together and laughed and talked. They became friends and had fun. King Tom learned to eat other things besides lemons. He learned to be nice and share and care. He improved his health and his mind and his heart. He was a happy king. And everyone loved him. The end.

Tom and Mia run inside. They leave the can and the frozen mosquitoes outside. They hope Mom can help them. They hope the mosquitoes do not wake up. They hope they do not get in trouble. They learned a lesson. They will not play with the freeze can again.

"No, Sam, don't eat the plant!" Tom says. "The plant is not food. The plant is for bees and birds. Eating the plant is bad. Eating the plant is stupid."

"Sam, are you okay?" Tom asks. He is worried. He is sorry. He hugs Sam. "I told you not to eat the plant. The plant is not for us. The plant is for nature. Next time, listen to me. Next time, be smart."

Sam nods. He is sad. He is sorry. He hugs Tom back. "You are right, Tom. Eating the plant was stupid. Eating the plant was a mistake. Next time, I will listen to you. Next time, I will be smart. Can we still be friends?"

"Of course, Sam, we can still be friends," Tom says. He smiles. He wipes Sam's tears. "Friends make mistakes. Friends say sorry. Friends help each other. Friends share. Do you want some of my apple? My apple is yummy. My apple is good for us."

Tom and Sam eat the apple together. They are happy. They are friends. They learn from their mistake. They do not eat plants anymore. They eat fruits and vegetables. They are smart. They are good.

Mommy said, "Yes, it's a pretty bird." 

Suddenly, a boy came and took Lily's blueberries. Lily was sad and cried. Mommy asked, "What happened, sweetie?" 

Lily said, "The boy took my yummy blueberries." 

Mommy said, "Let's talk to the boy and ask him to give them back." 

The boy said, "Sorry, I didn't know they were yours. Here you go." 

Lily was happy and thanked the boy. She ate her yummy blueberries and continued to see more blue things in the park.

Her mom said, "Okay, you can keep your blanket with you, but you need to give me the iron."

Max quickly ran back to his hole to hide. But when he got there, he saw that his family was all gone. Max was very sad and didn't know what to do. Just then, he heard a voice outside his hole.

Max peeked out and saw a friendly bird. "My family is gone and there's a dangerous cat outside," Max said. "I don't know what to do."

The bird thought for a moment and then said, "I have an idea. You can come live with me in my nest. It's high up in a tree, so the cat can't get you. And we can be friends!"

Max thought about it for a minute and then decided to go with the bird. He was so happy to have a new friend and a safe place to live. And that's how Max and the bird became the best of friends.

Once they arrived, they opened the box and the snake slithered away into the trees. Lily felt happy that the snake was safe and free.

One day, Lucy came home from school and ran to her room. She wanted to write about the new song she learned in music class. But when she lifted her bed, she saw that her journal was gone. She felt very sad and angry. Who took her journal?

Tom looked up and saw Lucy. He smiled and said, "Hi, Lucy. I found this book under your bed. It has funny pictures and words in it. I wanted to read it."

Lucy grabbed her journal from his backpack and said, "This is not a book, Tom. This is my journal. It is mine. You cannot read it. It is private."

Tom frowned and said, "But I like your journal, Lucy. It is interesting. Why can't I read it?"

Lucy felt a little sorry for Tom. She remembered that he was younger than her and did not understand what a journal was. She said, "Tom, a journal is a special book where you write your own thoughts and feelings. It is like a friend who listens to you. You do not read other people's journals, because they might have secrets or things they do not want to share. How would you feel if I read your diary?"

Tom thought for a moment. He had a diary where he drew his favorite animals and cars. He did not want Lucy to see it. He said, "I would feel bad, Lucy. I would feel like you did not respect me."

Lucy nodded and said, "That is how I feel, Tom. You did not respect me when you took my journal. You should ask me first if you want to see something that is mine. And you should say sorry."

Tom realized that he was wrong. He said, "I am sorry, Lucy. I did not mean to hurt you. I was just curious. Can we still be friends?"

Lucy smiled and said, "Of course, Tom. We are always friends. But next time, please do not take my things without asking. And maybe I can show you some of my journal if you promise not to tell anyone."

They tried to take the drum away from Max, but he held on to it. He said, "No, it's my turn! I want to play the drum!" Tom and Lily pulled and pushed, but Max did not let go. They started to shout and cry. Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong.

She saw them fighting over the drum and frowned. She said, "Stop it, you three! You are not being nice to each other. You have to share the drum and play together. The drum is not only yours, it is for everyone. How would you feel if someone took your toy away from you?"

Tom and Lily felt ashamed. They knew their mom was right. They said, "Sorry, mom. Sorry, Max. We were selfish. We will share the drum and play with you." Max smiled and said, "Thank you, Tom and Lily. You are dependable. You are good cousins." They hugged and made up.

They decided to play the drum together, and take turns to hit it and sing. They learned to listen to each other and have fun. Their mom was happy to see them get along. She said, "That's better. You are being kind and respectful. That's what family is for. I'm proud of you." They smiled and said, "We love you, mom. We love you, Max. We love the drum." They played the drum until it was time for dinner.

Lily and Max were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. They saw a big hill with lots of flowers. They wanted to roll down the hill.

"Let's go!" Max said. He ran to the hill and lay down. He started to roll. He felt the wind and the grass on his face. He laughed.

Lily followed him. She lay down and rolled too. She saw the sky and the trees spinning. She giggled.

But then they rolled too fast. They bumped into each other. They bumped into a rock. They bumped into a fence. They felt ouch and dizzy.

A lady came to help them. She was nice. She gave them water and a band-aid. She said, "You should be careful. Rolling down the hill is fun, but it can be dangerous. You could get hurt or lost. You should warn each other before you roll. And you should look where you are going. And you should stop before you reach the end of the hill."

Lily and Max nodded. They said, "Thank you. We are sorry. We will warn each other. We will look where we are going. We will stop before the end of the hill."

They hugged the lady. They hugged each other. They felt better. They still liked to roll down the hill, but they did it more slowly and safely. They had fun.

Lily and Ben liked to play with blocks. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes. They could make houses, towers, cars and animals with their blocks. They had a lot of fun.

One day, they decided to make a big castle with all their blocks. They found a table in the living room and put a big cloth over it. They said it was their castle wall. Then they started to add blocks on top of the cloth. They made windows, doors, flags and towers. They said it was their brilliant castle.

But they did not see that the table was old and weak. It had a crack in one of its legs. The more blocks they added, the more weight they put on the table. The table started to wobble and creak. Lily and Ben did not hear it. They were too busy adding more blocks.

Suddenly, the table broke. The leg with the crack snapped and the table fell down. The cloth and the blocks came crashing down with it. Lily and Ben screamed and ran away. They were scared and hurt. Some of the blocks hit them and made them bleed. The living room was a mess. The table was broken. The cloth was torn. The blocks were scattered.

Mom and Dad heard the noise and came running. They saw Lily and Ben crying and the living room ruined. They were angry and sad. They hugged Lily and Ben and took them to the bathroom. They cleaned their wounds and put bandages on them. They said they were glad they were not badly hurt. But they also said they were disappointed. They said Lily and Ben should have been more careful. They said they should have checked the table before putting so much weight on it. They said they should have listened to the sounds of the table. They said they should have stopped adding blocks when they saw the table was wobbling. They said they should have learned to be content with what they had. They said they should have respected the things they had and not ruined them. They said they should have been more responsible and wise.

Lily and Ben felt sorry and ashamed. They said they were sorry. They said they learned their lesson. They said they would not do it again. They said they would help Mom and Dad clean the living room and fix the table. They said they would be more careful and grateful next time. They said they would be better children.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big jar of peanuts on a bench. They were hungry and wanted to eat some.

"Who do you think left these peanuts here?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Maybe someone forgot them," Ben said.

"Should we take some? They look yummy," Lily said.

Ben looked around and saw no one. He felt tempted to grab a handful of peanuts. But then he remembered what his mom had taught him. He shook his head and said, "No, we shouldn't. That would be stealing. Stealing is bad. We have to be honest and respect other people's things."

Lily nodded and agreed. She said, "You're right, Ben. We have to be honest and kind. Maybe the owner of the peanuts will come back soon. Let's go play somewhere else."

They left the jar of peanuts alone and went to the swings. They had fun and felt good about themselves.

Soon, a man came back to the bench. He was looking for his jar of peanuts. He had left it there by mistake. He was happy to see that it was still there and no one had taken any. He smiled and said, "Thank you, whoever you are, for being honest and not taking my peanuts. You have made my day. I will share some of my peanuts with the squirrels as a reward."

The man opened the jar and threw some peanuts to the squirrels. The squirrels came and ate them happily. They thanked the man with their squeaks and tails.

Lily and Ben saw the man and the squirrels from afar. They smiled and felt proud of themselves. They had learned a valuable lesson: honesty is the best policy.

One day, Tom wanted to show his friends how brave he was. He saw a big snake sleeping on a branch. He thought he could scare the snake and make his friends laugh. He crept up to the snake and shouted, "Boo!"

But the snake was not scared. It opened its eyes and hissed at Tom. It was very angry and wanted to bite him. Tom was so afraid that he ran away as fast as he could. He tripped on a root and fell into a puddle of mud. He was wet and dirty and his clothes were torn.

His friends saw what happened and ran to help him. They were not laughing. They were worried and sorry for him. They helped him get up and cleaned him up. They told him that he should not bother the snake. It was dangerous and mean. They said he was lucky that the snake did not hurt him.

Tom felt very embarrassed. He realized that he was not brave, but foolish. He said sorry to his friends and to the snake. He learned his lesson and never tried to scare the snake again. He was happy that his friends were kind and forgiving. He hugged them and thanked them. They were still his friends and they still liked to play in the jungle.

One day, grandpa had to go to town for some work. He told the twins to stay near the house and not to bother Molly. He said Molly was tired and needed to rest. He made them promise to be good and listen to grandma. Lila and Ben nodded and said they would.

But after grandpa left, the twins got bored. They wanted to see Molly and have some fun. They thought Molly would not mind if they played with her for a little while. They sneaked out of the house and ran to the barn where Molly was sleeping.

They woke her up and asked her to play with them. Molly was not jolly. She was grumpy and wanted to sleep. She shook her head and tried to ignore them. But the twins did not listen. They climbed on her back, pulled her ears, and tickled her nose.

Molly had enough. She gave a loud bray and kicked her legs. She threw the twins off her back and ran out of the barn. She galloped across the field and did not stop until she reached the fence. She was angry and scared.

The twins were sad and sorry. They had broken their promise and hurt Molly. They ran after her and called her name. They said they were sorry and asked her to come back. They said they loved her and would not bother her again.

Molly heard them and looked back. She saw their tears and heard their words. She felt sorry for them too. She walked back to them and let them hug her. She licked their faces and nuzzled their hair. She was jolly again.

The twins were happy and grateful. They thanked Molly and said they would keep their promise. They said they would be good and listen to grandma. They walked back to the house with Molly and gave her some carrots. They said they would see her again tomorrow.

Sara and Tom knew they were in trouble. They quickly tried to hide the broken clock under the bed. They hoped their mom would not see it. Sara and Tom nodded and said, "Yes, mom." They went to pick up the pieces of the clock and the other toys. They wished they had not fought over the clock. They learned their lesson. They decided to be more tidy and more kind.

Lily and Ben were playing on the farm. They liked to run and jump and see the animals. They saw a big pile of hay and wanted to climb on it. They ran to the hay and started to make a fort.

"Look, I found a hole!" Lily said. She put her hand in the hole and felt something soft and warm. "What is it?" she asked.

Lily smiled and tried to pull the bunny out of the hole. But the bunny did not want to come out. It made a loud noise and bit Lily's finger. "Ow!" Lily cried. She let go of the bunny and held her finger. It was red and hurt.

Ben felt sorry for Lily. He wanted to help her. He looked for a band-aid or a cloth to wrap her finger. But he could not find anything. He felt confused and scared. What if Lily's finger got worse? What if the bunny had a disease?

He saw a farmer walking by and called him. "Mister, mister, please help us!" he said. "Lily got bit by a bunny and her finger is bleeding!"

The farmer heard Ben and came to see what was wrong. He saw Lily and Ben and the pile of hay. He saw the bunny in the hole. He understood what happened. He took Lily's hand and looked at her finger. He said, "Don't worry, kids, it's not a bad bite. The bunny was just scared and tried to protect itself. It's not a mean bunny. It's a baby bunny. It lives in the hay with its mother and siblings. Once there was a brave little boy named Andy. He went outside to explore the big world. As he was walking, he noticed something was flying very high in the sky. He stopped and stared, realizing that it was a bird. He wanted to fly as high as the bird, so he spread his arms like wings and began running really fast. He felt the wind blowing in his face, but he didn't lift up. He felt disappointed but he was brave.

Suddenly a kind old man appeared and said, "You have to have wings to be able to fly like the bird, don't you?"

Andy nodded and said, "Yes, I do have wings, they are just not visible."

The kind old man smiled and said, "I admire your bravery, but you will never realize your dream with no wings. To reach the sky, you need to use your two legs. You can use them to climb mountains or run as fast as a bird."

Andy was sad at first, but then he finally realized the kind old man was right. He thanked the old man for his wise words and promised he would no longer try to fly without wings.

The moral of the story is that we all have the potential to reach our dreams, but we need to be brave and use our legs to get there.

"Can we play together, Ben?" Lily asked.

"Sure, Lily. Let's pretend we are farmers and take care of our cow and horse," Ben said.

They smiled and ran to their toys. Mom watched them and smiled too. She was happy they learned to appreciate their differences and get along.

He drives his truck to the flower. He stops and gets out. He reaches for the flower. But then he hears a buzz buzz. He sees a black and yellow bug on the flower. It is a bee. Ben is scared of bees. He thinks they will sting him.

He runs back to his truck. He gets in and drives away. He leaves the flower and the bee alone. He decides he will not pick it. He will find another gift for his mom. Maybe a rock or a stick or a leaf. He thinks she will like them too. He smiles and makes his truck go vroom vroom and honk honk. He loves his truck.

Tom and Lily are playing with their toys in the living room. Tom has a big truck that can lift things with a hook. Lily has a small car that can zoom very fast. They like to make noises and pretend they are on a road.

"Look, Lily, I can lift this ball with my truck. It is very heavy, but my truck is very strong," Tom says, making a vroom-vroom sound.

"That is cool, Tom, but can your truck zoom like my car? My car is very fast, and it can go under the sofa and the table," Lily says, making a beep-beep sound.

They take turns showing each other what their toys can do. They have fun and laugh a lot. Then, they see a new toy on the shelf. It is a shiny rocket that has wings and a button.

"Wow, what is that?" Tom asks, pointing at the rocket.

"I don't know, but it looks original. Maybe it can fly to the moon," Lily says, reaching for the rocket.

They take the rocket and examine it. They see a sticker that says "Press here". They press the button and the rocket makes a loud zoom sound. It also lights up and shakes.

"Wow, it is alive!" Tom says, holding the rocket.

"Let's play with it. Maybe it can lift us to the sky," Lily says, holding Tom's hand.

They run to the backyard with the rocket. They pretend they are astronauts and the rocket is their spaceship. They have a blast.

One day, Lily and Ben want to play with each other's tubes. Lily asks Ben to give her his small tube. Ben says no. He likes his small tube. He does not want to share. Lily gets mad. She tries to grab his small tube. Ben pulls it away. They start to fight.

Mom hears them fighting. She comes to the living room. She sees them pulling and pushing. She is not happy. She tells them to stop. She says they have to share their toys. She says they have to be nice to each other. She says they have to serve each other.

Lily and Ben nod. They agree. They like to be clean. They like to serve. They like to play. They love each other. They love Mom. They are happy twins. The end.

"Let's unlock the door and go in," Tom said. He found a key under a rock. He put the key in the lock and turned it. The door opened.

"Wow, look at all the things in here," Lily said. She saw pots and pans, jars and bottles, books and toys. She picked up a bottle with a red label. It smelled spicy.

"I wonder what this is," she said. She opened the bottle and took a sip.

"Yuck, this is hot!" she cried. She dropped the bottle and ran to the door. But the door was locked again.

"Help, help, let us out!" she shouted.

Tom tried to find the key, but he could not see it. It was under the spilled bottle. The spicy liquid was burning his eyes and nose.

"Who is there?" a voice said. It was an old woman with a big nose and a black hat. She was the owner of the hut. She was a witch.

"You naughty children, you broke into my hut and drank my potion. Now you will pay the price," she said. She waved her hand and turned Lily and Tom into frogs.

She put them in a cage and hung it on the wall. She laughed and said, "Now you will be my pets. You will never unlock the door again."

"Sure, but you have to pay. One ice cream or one candy is one dollar," the man said.

"That is not nice. That is stealing. The man worked hard for the coins. We should not take them," Anna whispered back.

"Here, Anna. You can have this. I have the ice cream," he said.

Tommy was a little cat who liked to spend his days playing outside. He was adventurous and curious, and always wanted to see new things. One day, he saw a big tree with many birds on it. He wanted to climb the tree and catch a bird.

He ran to the tree and jumped on the lowest branch. He used his paws to hold on and move up. He saw a blue bird with a shiny feather. He tried to reach it, but the bird flew away. Tommy followed it to another branch, and then another. He was so busy chasing the bird that he did not notice how high he was.

"Tommy, Tommy, where are you?" his mother called from the ground. She was looking for him, but she could not see him. She was worried that he was lost or in trouble.

"Here, mama, here!" Tommy meowed from the top of the tree. He looked down and saw his mother. She looked very small and far away. He realized that he was very high and he felt scared. He did not know how to get down.

"Tommy, you are too high! You have to come down, now!" his mother said. "Be careful, do not fall!"

Tommy wanted to go down, but he did not know how. He looked around, but he could not find a way. He started to cry. He wished he had not been so adventurous.

"Mama, mama, help me!" he cried.

His mother heard him and tried to calm him. She said, "Do not worry, Tommy, I will help you. Just stay where you are and do not move. I will get someone to help you."

She ran to the house and called Mr. Brown, the farmer who lived next door. He had a big ladder and a big hat. He came quickly and put the ladder against the tree. He climbed up the ladder and reached Tommy. He put his hat on Tommy's head and said, "Hello, little cat. You are a brave one, but you have to be more careful. Do not climb so high, it is dangerous. Now, let me take you down."

He picked up Tommy and put him in his hat. He held the hat with one hand and the ladder with the other. He climbed down slowly and carefully. He gave Tommy to his mother, who hugged him and thanked him.

"Thank you, Mr. Brown, you are very kind. I am sorry for the trouble," she said.

"It is no trouble, Mrs. Cat. I am glad I could help. Tommy is a good cat, but he has to learn his limits. Maybe next time he will be more cautious," he said.

He smiled and waved goodbye. He took his ladder and his hat and went back to his house.

Tommy was happy to be safe and with his mother. He was sorry for being so adventurous and making her worry. He said, "I am sorry, mama. I will not climb so high again. I love you, mama."

"I love you too, Tommy. I am glad you are okay. But you have to be more careful, Tommy. You have to listen to me and do not go too far. You have to be a good cat, Tommy," she said.

She licked his fur and cuddled him. She took him to their house and gave him some milk and some fish. He drank and ate and felt better. He learned his lesson and decided to be more careful. He still liked to play outside, but he did not chase birds or climb trees anymore. He was a good cat, Tommy.

Tim was not happy. He wanted to make a bigger bubble than Mia. He dipped his wand again and blew harder. But he blew too hard and his bubble popped. He tried again and again, but his bubbles kept popping. He got angry and threw his wand on the ground.

Mia saw Tim's tantrum and felt sorry for him. She walked over to him and said, "Don't be mad, Tim. It's just a game. We can share the soap and have fun together."

Tim looked at Mia and saw her kind face. He felt ashamed of his behavior. He picked up his wand and said, "I'm sorry, Mia. You're right. It's just a game. Can we share the soap and have fun together?"

Mia nodded and smiled. She gave Tim a hug and said, "Of course we can. You're my brother and I love you."

They both dipped their wands in the soap and blew gently. They made many bubbles of different sizes and shapes. They laughed and chased the bubbles in the air. They were happy and had fun together.

The moral of the story is: Don't be jealous of others. Be kind and share. You will have more fun and succeed in making friends.

"What do you want from us?" Ben asked.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big mountain far away. They wanted to go there and see what was on top.

"Let's go to the mountain!" Ben said.

"OK, but we have to be careful," Lily said. "Mom and Dad warned us not to go too far."

They put on their hats and shoes and started to walk. They saw many things on the way: flowers, birds, cars, and people. The mountain looked closer and closer.

"Wow, it's so big and tall!" Ben said.

"Look, there are some rocks and trees on it," Lily said.

They reached the foot of the mountain and saw a path that went up. They decided to follow it. They climbed and climbed, but the mountain was very steep and hard. They got tired and thirsty.

"Maybe we should go back," Lily said. "It's getting late and we don't have any water."

"But I want to see the top," Ben said. "Maybe there is something cool there."

He kept going, but Lily stopped. She was worried. She looked around and saw that they were very high. She also saw that the path was very narrow and had a big drop on one side. She was scared.

"Ben, come back!" she shouted. "It's too dangerous!"

But Ben did not hear her. He was too busy looking at the top. He did not see that the path was slippery and had some loose rocks. He stepped on one and slipped. He screamed and fell.

Lily ran to him and grabbed his hand. She pulled him up and hugged him. He was crying and bleeding.

"I'm sorry, Lily," he said. "You were right. We should have listened to Mom and Dad."

"It's OK, Ben," she said. "I'm glad you're OK. Let's go home now."

They held hands and walked down the mountain. They were sorry and scared. They hoped Mom and Dad would not be angry. They learned their lesson. They never went to the mountain again.

Lily felt sad and hurt by Tom's words. She liked her car, even if it was not flashy. She tried to ignore Tom and play by herself.

Soon, Tom's car stopped lighting up and making sounds. He looked at the bottom and saw a small door. He opened it and saw two small round things inside. They were batteries. He took them out and tried to put them back in, but nothing happened. His car was broken.

"Hey, Lily, can you help me?" Tom asked, holding his car. "My car is not working. Do you have any batteries?"

Lily looked at Tom and remembered how he was mean to her. She felt angry and wanted to say no. But she also felt sorry for Tom and wanted to be kind. She thought of a creative idea.

"Sure, Tom, I can help you. But first, you have to say sorry for being rude to me and my car. And you have to play nicely with me and share your car. Then I will give you some batteries." Lily said, smiling.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge others by their appearance. Be kind and respectful to your friends. Share and help each other.

But then, Max remembered his collar and believed that he could do it. He tried again and this time it was easy. Max was so happy and proud of himself. From that day on, Max believed that he could do anything he wanted to do.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside and get dirty. One day, his mom asked him to clean his room. But Timmy didn't want to clean, he wanted to play. 

His mom said, "Timmy, you need to act responsible and clean your room."

Timmy groaned and started to clean. He saw a clock on his shelf and thought it was dirty. He wanted to clean it too. 

After he finished cleaning, Timmy's mom came to check his room. She was happy to see it was clean and said, "Good job, Timmy! You acted responsible and cleaned your room. Remember, it's important to keep things clean and tidy." 

From that day on, Timmy learned to act responsible and keep his things clean, including the clock on his shelf.

As Timmy was walking, he saw a cute little rabbit hopping around. He wanted to catch it, so he started running after it. But he didn't see the big hole in the ground and he fell in. 

Timmy hurt his leg and couldn't get out of the hole. He cried and cried until his mom found him. She was very sad that Timmy got hurt. She helped him out of the hole and took him to the hospital. Timmy learned that sometimes being adventurous can be dangerous, but he still loved his red coat and going on adventures.

"Can I ring it first?" Lily asks.

"No, I want to ring it first!" Tom says.

They both pull the phone. They are angry and loud. The phone falls on the ground. It breaks. They hear a sad sound.

"Oh no, what did we do?" Lily says.

"We broke the phone. It was not ours. It was bad," Tom says.

They feel sorry. They see a man coming. He is wearing a blue hat. He looks at the phone. He looks at them.

"Did you break my phone?" he asks.

"Yes, we did. We are sorry. We wanted to ring it. We did not share. We did not use our words," Lily says.

The man is not happy. He is not mad. He is calm.

"I see. Well, I am glad you told me the truth. That is good. But you should not touch things that are not yours. That is bad. And you should share and use your words. That is good. Do you understand?" he says.

"Yes, we understand. We are sorry. We will share and use our words next time," Tom says.

The man nods. He picks up the phone. He leaves. Lily and Tom hug. They are friends again. They learned a lesson. They go to play with other toys and books. They are happy and quiet.

"Sorry, mom," Ben says.

"It's okay, sweeties," Mom says. "We can fix it. Let's find another envelope and write the address again. Then we can put your picture inside the envelope and send it to grandma. She will love it!"

Tom is a horse who lives on a farm. He likes to run and play with his friends, the cows and the sheep. He also likes to eat hay, which is dry grass that the farmer gives him. Hay is tasty and good for Tom.

One day, Tom sees a big pile of hay in the barn. He thinks it is for him, so he runs to it and starts to eat. He does not see the sign that says "Cover for the carrots". The farmer is growing carrots in the field, and he needs the hay to cover them when it is cold. The hay keeps the carrots warm and safe.

The farmer sees Tom eating the hay and gets angry. He shouts at Tom and tells him to stop. He says the hay is not for him, it is for the carrots. He says Tom is being greedy and naughty. He says Tom has to leave the barn and go back to his pen.

Tom feels sad and sorry. He did not know the hay was for the carrots. He did not mean to be greedy and naughty. He wants to be useful and help the farmer. He thinks of a way to make up for his mistake.

He runs to the field and finds the carrots. He sees some hay that he did not eat. He picks it up with his mouth and carries it to the carrots. He covers the carrots with the hay, one by one. He works hard and fast, until all the carrots are covered.

The farmer sees what Tom is doing and smiles. He is not angry anymore. He says Tom is being smart and kind. He says Tom is helping him and the carrots. He says Tom is a good and useful horse. He gives Tom a hug and a carrot.

Tom is happy and proud. He likes the carrot and the hug. He likes to be smart and kind. He likes to help the farmer and the carrots. He likes to be a good and useful horse. He goes back to his pen and tells his friends what he did. They all clap and cheer for Tom.

Lila was a humble girl who liked to help her mom and dad. She did not have many toys, but she was happy with what she had. She loved to watch the pigeons in the park and feed them bread crumbs.

One day, it was Lila's birthday. Her mom and dad gave her a big hug and a small cake with three candles. They sang happy birthday to her and let her blow out the candles. Lila made a wish, but she did not tell anyone what it was.

After the cake, they went to the park to play. Lila saw a pigeon with a shiny ring on its leg. She thought it was very pretty and wanted to touch it. She walked slowly towards the pigeon, holding out her hand with some bread crumbs. The pigeon did not fly away. It came closer and ate the bread crumbs from her hand. Lila felt very happy and smiled.

The pigeon looked at Lila with its bright eyes and cooed softly. It lifted its leg and showed Lila the ring. Lila saw that the ring had a small tag with a name and a number. She read the name: Flora. She read the number: 555-1234.

Lila realized that the pigeon was someone's pet and that they must be looking for it. She felt sorry for the pigeon and its owner. She decided to do a good thing and call the number. She asked her mom for her phone and dialed the number.

A voice answered: "Hello?"

Lila said: "Hi, I found your pigeon. Her name is Flora. She has a ring on her leg. She is in the park with me. Do you want her back?"

The voice said: "Oh, thank you so much! You are very kind. I have been looking for Flora for a long time. She flew away from her cage and I was very worried. Where are you in the park? I will come and get her right away."

Lila told the voice where she was and waited for the owner to come. The owner was a nice lady who hugged Lila and thanked her again. She gave Lila a small gift: a necklace with a pigeon charm. She said: "This is for you, to remember Flora and to celebrate your birthday. You are a very humble and generous girl. Flora and I are very lucky to meet you."

Lila felt very proud and happy. She put on the necklace and said goodbye to Flora and the lady. She went back to her mom and dad and told them what happened. They praised her for her good deed and hugged her. They said: "We are very proud of you, Lila. You have a big heart and a good spirit. You are the best birthday girl ever."

Her mom said, "No, Lily. The bees might sting you if you go too close. They do not like people who touch their honey. Stay here with me and Spot."

But Lily did not listen to her mom. She thought the bees would not mind if she just took a peek. She sneaked away from her mom and Spot and walked towards the tree. She saw a hole in the hive where the honey was dripping. She reached out her hand to touch the honey.

But the bees saw her and got angry. They flew out of the hive and buzzed around Lily. They stung her hand and her face. Lily screamed and ran back to her mom and Spot. She was crying and hurting.
