Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play with balloons. They had many balloons of different colors and shapes. They liked to blow them up, tie them, and make them fly in the air. Sometimes they would pop them and laugh at the loud noise.

One day, they got a new balloon from their mom. It was a modern balloon that could change colors and make sounds. It was very shiny and pretty. Anna and Ben wanted to play with it, but they could not agree on who would go first.

"I want it!" Anna shouted. "No, I want it!" Ben shouted. They pulled the balloon from each other, trying to take it away. The balloon did not like being pulled. It made a sad sound and turned gray.

"Stop it!" their mom shouted. "You are hurting the balloon and each other. You need to share and take turns. That is how you play nicely and have fun."

Anna and Ben felt sorry. They did not want to hurt the balloon or their mom. They let go of the balloon and hugged each other. They said sorry and agreed to share and take turns. The balloon liked that. It made a happy sound and turned rainbow.

Anna and Ben played with the balloon together. They made it fly, change colors, and make sounds. They had a lot of fun and thanked their mom for the modern balloon. They learned that sharing is caring and that it is better to play nicely than to shout.

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play together. But sometimes they fight over toys.

One day, they are having lunch. Mom gives them rice and soup. Lily likes rice. She eats it fast. Tom does not like rice. He plays with it.

"Tom, eat your rice," Mom says. "It is good for you."

"No, I don't want rice," Tom says. He makes a face. He throws some rice on the floor.

Lily is angry. She loves rice. She thinks Tom is wasting it. She grabs Tom's bowl. She tries to eat his rice.

"Hey, stop it!" Tom shouts. He pulls the bowl back. He spills some soup on Lily's dress.

Lily cries. She is wet and sticky. She runs to Mom. "Tom is bad! He threw rice and soup on me!"

Mom is alert. She hears the noise. She sees the mess. She is not happy. She closes her eyes. She takes a deep breath.

"Lily, Tom, come here," Mom says. "You need to say sorry to each other. And you need to help me clean up. Rice and soup are not toys. They are food. You should not waste them or fight over them. Do you understand?"

Lily and Tom nod. They feel sorry. They hug each other. They say sorry to Mom. They help her wipe the floor and the table. They finish their lunch. They promise to be nice to each other. Mom smiles. She gives them a kiss. She says she loves them.

Sara and Ben were playing with their blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and bridges and houses. They used different colors and shapes to make their blocks look nice.

"Look, Sara, I made a number with my blocks!" Ben said. He showed her his blocks that looked like a four. "Four is my favorite number. How many blocks do you have?"

Sara counted her blocks. She had six blocks. "I have six blocks, Ben. Six is more than four. Six is a bigger number."

Ben did not like that. He wanted to have more blocks than Sara. He wanted to have the biggest number. He grabbed two of Sara's blocks and added them to his own. "Now I have six blocks, too. And you have four. We have the same number."

Sara was angry. Ben took her blocks without asking. He was not nice. She wanted her blocks back. She pulled on the blocks that Ben took. "No, Ben, those are my blocks! Give them back to me!"

Ben pulled back. He did not want to give them back. He liked having six blocks. He liked having the same number as Sara. He shouted at Sara. "No, Sara, they are my blocks now! I want them!"

They pulled and pulled on the blocks. They did not share. They did not listen. They did not stop.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise outside. They looked out the window and saw a big storm. The wind was blowing hard. The rain was falling fast. The sky was dark. It was a hurricane.

They were scared. They forgot about their blocks. They ran to their mom and dad, who were in the kitchen. They hugged them tight.

Mom and dad told them not to worry. They said they were safe in their house. They said the hurricane would go away soon. They said they loved them.

Sara and Ben felt better. They realized that their blocks were not important. They realized that they were silly to fight. They realized that they loved each other.

They said sorry to each other. They hugged each other. They went back to their blocks. They shared them. They made a new number with their blocks. They made a ten. Ten was a bigger number than six. Ten was a light number. Ten was a happy number.

Lily and Max were best friends. They liked to play with dolls and cars and books. One day, they found a big bag in the closet. It had a zipper on it. They opened the zipper and saw many pretty things inside.

Lily saw a shiny necklace. She wanted to wear it. She took it out of the bag and put it around her neck. Max saw a funny hat. He wanted to wear it. He took it out of the bag and put it on his head. They looked at each other and laughed.

But then, they heard a voice. It was Mom. She was coming to the closet. She sounded angry. Lily and Max got scared. They tried to put the things back in the bag. But they were too late. Mom opened the closet and saw them.

"What are you doing?" Mom asked. "This is not your bag. This is Grandma's bag. She gave it to me. These are her things. You should not touch them. You could break them or lose them. You are very naughty."

Lily and Max felt bad. They did not know it was Grandma's bag. They did not mean to be naughty. They were sorry. They looked at Mom with sad eyes.

"Mom, we are sorry," Lily said. "We did not know. We just wanted to play. Please don't be mad at us."

"Mom, we are sorry," Max said. "We did not know. We just wanted to have fun. Please forgive us."

Mom looked at Lily and Max. She saw that they were sorry. She saw that they were smart. They knew they did something wrong. They said they were sorry. They asked for forgiveness. Mom loved Lily and Max. She was not mad at them anymore.

"OK, I forgive you," Mom said. "But you have to be more careful. You have to ask before you touch things that are not yours. You have to respect Grandma's things. They are very special to her and to me. Do you understand?"

Lily and Max nodded. They understood. They hugged Mom and said they loved her. Mom hugged them back and said she loved them too. She helped them put the things back in the bag. She closed the zipper. She put the bag back in the closet. She took Lily and Max to the living room. They played with their own toys and had a good time. They were happy. They were best friends.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toy trucks in the garden. They liked to make loud noises and pretend they were driving on the road. Tom had a big red truck and Lily had a small yellow truck.

"Look at my truck, it is faster than yours!" Tom said to Lily. He pushed his truck hard and it zoomed across the grass.

"No, my truck is faster and smarter!" Lily said to Tom. She pushed her truck harder and it zoomed past Tom's truck.

They were having fun, but they did not see the big hole in the ground. It was near the fence and it was very deep and dangerous. Someone had dug it to fix a pipe, but they had not covered it up.

Tom's truck was going so fast that it went over the edge of the hole and fell down. Tom was scared and ran to the hole. He looked down and saw his truck lying on the dirt. He wanted to get it back, but he knew it was too dangerous to go down.

"Lily, help me! My truck is in the hole!" Tom cried.

Lily heard Tom and ran to the hole. She saw Tom's truck and felt sorry for him. She wanted to help him, but she did not know how.

"Tom, don't go down, it is dangerous! You might get hurt!" Lily said.

"But I want my truck! It is my favorite toy!" Tom said.

Lily thought hard and had an idea. She ran to the shed and got a long rope. She tied one end to the fence and threw the other end into the hole. She hoped it would reach Tom's truck.

"Tom, look! I have a rope! Maybe you can use it to get your truck!" Lily said.

Tom looked at the rope and smiled. He was glad Lily was so smart and kind. He grabbed the rope and pulled it until he felt his truck. He tied the rope around his truck and shouted to Lily.

"Lily, I have it! Pull the rope!" Tom said.

Lily pulled the rope with all her strength. She saw Tom's truck coming up from the hole. She was happy and proud. She helped Tom get his truck out of the hole and gave it to him.

"Here is your truck, Tom! Are you happy?" Lily said.

"Yes, I am very happy! Thank you, Lily! You are the best friend ever!" Tom said.

They hugged and smiled. They decided to play with their trucks somewhere else, away from the hole. They learned to be careful and to help each other. They had a lot of fun with their trucks.

Sam and Mia liked to play with their toys in their room. They had many toys, like cars, dolls, blocks and books. They also had a big window that showed them the city. The city had many tall buildings that looked modern and shiny.

One day, while they were playing, they heard a loud noise. It was like a big roar. The floor started to shake and the toys fell down. Sam and Mia were scared and hugged each other. They looked out the window and saw that the buildings were moving and breaking. Some of them fell down and made dust and smoke. They saw people running and screaming.

Sam and Mia wanted to go to their mom and dad, but they could not. The door was stuck and they could not open it. They tried to call for help, but no one heard them. They felt more shaking and more noise. They saw a big crack appear in the wall. The crack got bigger and bigger, until the wall broke and the room fell apart. Sam and Mia fell with it and did not get up. The end.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to hide behind the trees and bushes and scare each other. They made funny noises and faces and laughed a lot.

But then they heard a loud roar from the house. It was their uncle. He was angry because they had spilled his coffee on the table. His coffee was bitter and he did not like it. He came out of the house and looked for them.

"Where are you, you naughty children?" he shouted. "You made a big mess and you will have to clean it up!"

Lily and Ben were scared of their uncle. He was big and loud and mean. They did not want to face him. They ran to the other side of the garden and hid behind a fence.

"Please don't find us, please don't find us," they whispered to each other.

But their uncle was not so smart. He did not see them behind the fence. He walked around the garden and looked under the flowers and the rocks. He did not find them. He got tired and bored and went back to the house.

Lily and Ben waited until he was gone. Then they came out of their hiding place and hugged each other.

"We are safe, we are safe," they said. "We are sorry we spilled his coffee, but he did not have to scare us like that."

They decided to go inside and say sorry to their uncle and help him clean the table. They hoped he would be nicer to them and maybe give them a cookie. They also hoped he would make a new coffee for himself, but not so bitter.

Tim and Mia are bored. They want to play a game. They ask Mom for an idea.

Mom says, "Why don't you play hide and seek? I will count to ten and you can hide anywhere in the house. Then I will search for you."

Tim and Mia like this game. They run to find good hiding places. Tim hides under the bed. Mia hides behind the chair.

Mom counts to ten and then says, "Ready or not, here I come!" She looks in the living room, the kitchen, and the bathroom. She does not see Tim or Mia.

She goes to the bedroom and sees a lump under the bed. She says, "I found you, Tim! You are not very sneaky." Tim giggles and comes out.

She looks around and does not see Mia. She says, "Where is Mia? Is she in the closet?" She opens the closet and sees only clothes.

She says, "Is she under the desk?" She looks under the desk and sees only books.

She says, "Is she behind the chair?" She moves the chair and sees Mia. Mia says, "Boo!" and laughs.

Mom says, "I found you, Mia! You are very clever." Mia smiles and hugs Mom.

Mom says, "You are both good at hiding. But now it is your turn to search for me. I will hide and you can count to ten."

Tim and Mia say, "Okay!" They start to count and Mom runs to hide. They are not bored anymore. They have fun playing hide and seek.

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to pretend they were knights and princesses. Ben had a toy sword and Lily had a crown.

"Look, Lily, I found a dragon!" Ben said, pointing to a big lizard on a rock. "I will save you from it!"

He ran towards the lizard with his sword, but the lizard was not afraid. It hissed and opened its mouth, showing its sharp teeth.

"Ben, be careful!" Lily shouted. She was worried for her brother. She did not want him to get hurt by the lizard.

Ben tried to hit the lizard with his sword, but the lizard was too fast. It jumped and bit Ben's hand. Ben cried out in pain and dropped his sword.

"Ow, ow, ow! It bit me!" Ben said, holding his hand. "Lily, help me!"

Lily ran to Ben and hugged him. She saw blood on his hand. She was scared.

"Let go of him, you mean lizard!" she said to the lizard. She picked up Ben's sword and waved it at the lizard. The lizard did not like the sword. It let go of Ben's hand and ran away.

Lily threw the sword on the ground and looked at Ben's hand. She saw a small wound.

"Ben, are you okay?" she asked.

Ben nodded. He was still crying, but he felt better with Lily by his side.

"Thank you, Lily. You are a brave princess. You saved me from the dragon," he said.

Lily smiled. She was happy she helped her brother.

"You are welcome, Ben. You are a brave knight. You fought the dragon," she said.

They hugged each other and went inside to show their mom Ben's hand. Mom cleaned the wound and put a band-aid on it. She gave them both a kiss and a cookie.

They felt better and decided to play something else. They did not want to see the lizard again.

Tom and Anna are playing in the park. They see a big fire truck with a loud siren. The fire truck stops near a house that has smoke and flames. Tom and Anna are scared and curious.

"Look, Anna, the firemen are spraying water on the fire. They are brave and strong," Tom says.

"Yes, Tom, they are. But why is the house on fire? Did someone make a mistake?" Anna asks.

"I don't know, Anna. Maybe they left a candle or a stove on. Or maybe there was a storm and a lightning hit the house," Tom guesses.

They watch the firemen work hard to put out the fire. They see some people come out of the house. They look sad and scared. They hug each other and talk to the firemen. Tom and Anna feel sorry for them.

"Tom, look, there is a cat on the roof. It is black and white. It is scared too. It is meowing loudly. Do you think the firemen can save it?" Anna points.

"Wow, Anna, you are right. There is a cat. It is incredible that it is still alive. Maybe it ran away from the fire and climbed up there. I hope the firemen can save it. It needs a home and a family," Tom says.

They see a fireman with a ladder and a net. He climbs up the ladder and tries to catch the cat. The cat is scared and runs away from him. He follows the cat and talks to it softly. He finally catches the cat and puts it in the net. He climbs down the ladder and gives the cat to a lady. The lady is one of the people who came out of the house. She is happy and grateful. She hugs the cat and the fireman. She thanks him for saving her cat.

"Look, Anna, the fireman saved the cat. The cat belongs to the lady. She is happy. The cat is happy. The fireman is happy. We are happy too," Tom says.

"Yes, Tom, we are. The fireman is a hero. The cat is lucky. The lady is kind. The fire is out. The house is not good. It is burned and has ash. But the people and the cat are safe. That is good," Anna says.

They clap their hands and cheer for the fireman and the cat. They smile and hug each other. They are glad that the fire is over and that everyone is okay. They are friends and they care. They are good.

Tim and Mia went to the zoo with their mom. They liked to see the animals and learn their names. They saw lions, monkeys, elephants and many more. They were happy and excited.

But when they came to the pool where the seals lived, they saw that the water was dirty and the seals looked sad. There was no sun and the sky was gloomy. Tim and Mia felt sorry for the seals.

"Why are the seals so gloomy, mom?" Tim asked.

"Maybe they are bored or lonely, or they miss their home in the sea," mom said.

"Can we do something to make them happy?" Mia asked.

Mom thought for a moment. Then she said, "Maybe we can play a game with them. Do you know how to play guess?"

Tim and Mia nodded. They liked to play guess. It was a fun game where they had to think of something and the other person had to ask questions and guess what it was.

"OK, let's play guess with the seals. You can think of something and I will ask the seals questions. If they nod or clap, it means yes. If they shake their heads or bark, it means no. Let's see if they can guess what you are thinking of," mom said.

Tim and Mia agreed. They took turns to think of something and mom asked the seals questions. The seals seemed to understand and they started to nod, clap, shake their heads and bark. They also made funny faces and splashed water. Tim and Mia laughed and clapped. The seals looked happier and more lively.

The game went on for a while. The seals guessed many things, like a ball, a fish, a flower and a star. Then it was Mia's turn to think of something.

"I have something in my mind. It is big and round and yellow. It makes me warm and bright. What is it?" Mia said.

Mom asked the seals, "Is it something you can eat?"

The seals shook their heads.

"Is it something you can touch?"

The seals shook their heads again.

"Is it something you can see in the sky?"

The seals nodded and clapped.

"Is it the sun?" mom asked.

The seals nodded and clapped louder. They also barked and jumped in the water. They guessed right!

Mia smiled and said, "Yes, it is the sun. I wish the sun would come out and make the sky less gloomy."

As if by magic, the clouds parted and a ray of sunshine shone on the pool. The water sparkled and the seals glowed. Tim and Mia cheered and hugged mom. The seals cheered and hugged each other. They were all happy and grateful for the sun.

The end.

The kids started to play with the box. They took turns and shared the box. They pretended it was a car, a boat, and even a house. They all had lots of fun playing together. The kids learned that sharing and taking turns made everyone happy.

The moral of the story is that when we share and take turns, everyone can have fun and be happy.

As they went up, Wiggly saw a big bird. The bird looked at Wiggly and said, "Hello, little worm. What are you doing up here?" Wiggly said, "I am climbing the tree with my friend Ant." The bird smiled and said, "Oh, that's fun. Be careful, little worm."

Wiggly and Ant kept climbing. But the tree was very tall and it was not easy. Wiggly was tired. He leaned on Ant, but Ant was also tired. They both fell down from the tree.

Wiggly and Ant were hurt. They could not play anymore. The big bird came down and ate Wiggly. Ant was very sad. He learned that climbing a tree is not easy and can be dangerous.

"Tom, do not drink it," she said. "It is old and bad. It will make you sick. It is rot."

Tom did not listen to Lila. He wanted to be brave and try new things. He took a sip of the coffee. He spat it out.

"Blech! It is bitter and sour. It is rot!" he cried.

He threw the cup away. He ran to the hose and washed his mouth. He felt sorry and silly.

Lila came to him. She gave him a hug.

"It is okay, Tom," she said. "You made a mistake. But you learned something. Next time, listen to me. I am wise. I know things."

Tom nodded. He smiled.

"Thank you, Lila," he said. "You are wise. You are my friend."

They went back to playing. They left the can alone. They did not want to find any more coffee. They liked water and juice better.

Later, they played hide and seek. Tom hid behind a big chair. Lily looked all around, trying to find him. Then, she peeked behind the chair and saw Tom. "Found you, Tom!" she giggled. Tom meowed and jumped out from his hiding spot. They laughed and played until it was time for bed.

The next day, Spot went to the hole to get his bone. He dug and dug until he found the rough bone. Spot was so happy to have his bone back. He played with the bone all day and then put it back in the hole to keep it safe. Spot was a very happy dog.

One day, a helpful dog named Max went for a jog in the park. He loved to run and play with his friends. While jogging, Max saw a little girl named Lily. She looked sad and lost. Max wanted to help her.

"Come with me," Max said to Lily. "I will take you to your mom." Lily smiled and followed Max. They jogged together, looking for Lily's mom. They asked other animals in the park if they had seen her, but no one knew where she was.

Finally, they found a big tree. Max thought it was a good place to rest. But, when they sat down, a big branch fell from the tree. It hit Max and he was hurt. Lily cried and hugged Max. They never found Lily's mom that day.

The moral of the story is to always be careful when trying to help others. Sometimes, even helpful actions can lead to bad endings.

Anna and Ben want to hug the baby elephant too. They ask their dad if they can get out of the car and go closer. Their dad says no, it is not safe. The elephants are wild and might get scared or angry. He says they can only watch from a distance and be quiet.

Lily was a little rabbit who loved to spring. She would spring up and down, left and right, all over the meadow. She liked to see how high and far she could go. She did not listen to her mother, who told her to stay close to the burrow and not to go too far.

One day, Lily saw a big hill in the west. She wondered what was on the other side. She thought it would be fun to spring over the hill and explore. She did not tell her mother where she was going. She just sprang away, faster and faster, until she reached the top of the hill.

But when she looked down, she saw a big forest with many trees and shadows. She did not see any other rabbits or flowers or grass. She only saw strange noises and eyes. She felt scared and alone. She wished she had listened to her mother and stayed in the meadow.

She turned around and tried to spring back, but the hill was too steep and slippery. She fell and rolled and bumped and hurt herself. She cried and cried, hoping someone would hear her and help her.

Luckily, her mother had followed her tracks and found her. She hugged her and licked her and carried her back to the burrow. She gave her some tasty carrots and lettuce and water. She told her that she loved her and that she should always be careful and obey. Lily said she was sorry and that she learned her lesson. She never sprang away again without telling her mother. She was happy and safe in the meadow.

The bird and the bear became best friends. They hugged each other and played together every day. They sang happy songs and walked through the forest. And they lived happily ever after.

As she walked, the tray was very high and heavy. She met her brother Tom in the hallway. Tom said, "Amy, let me help you with that tray. It's too high for you." But Amy said, "No, I can do it!" She wanted to show that she was a big girl.

Amy tried to walk with the high tray, but it was too much for her. The tray fell, and the toys went everywhere. Amy was sad and cried. Tom came and said, "It's okay, Amy. We can pick up the toys together." They picked up the toys, and Amy learned that it is good to ask for help when things are too hard.

Once upon a time, there was a bald bird named Bob. Bob had a long neck and loved to play with his friends. One day, Bob and his friends were playing a game called "Guess the Animal."

"Guess what I am!" said one of Bob's friends. He made a funny noise and flapped his wings. "Are you a duck?" Bob asked. "Yes, good guess!" his friend replied.

Next, it was Bob's turn to make his friends guess. He stretched out his long neck and made a sound like "honk!" His friends thought for a moment. "Are you a goose?" asked one friend. "Yes, I am a goose!" Bob said with a big smile.

They played "Guess the Animal" all day long. Bob and his friends had lots of fun guessing and learning about different animals. At the end of the day, they all went back to their nests, tired but happy from their fun day of playing.

Once upon a time, there was a tidy town. In this town, there was a big post. Every day, people would march to the post. They would put their letters in the post. The post would send the letters to friends and family far away.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to march to the post. He had a letter for his grandma. He asked his mom, "Can I go to the post?" His mom said, "Yes, but be careful and march in a straight line."

Tim marched to the post. He saw other kids playing and wanted to join them. But he remembered his mom's words. He marched in a straight line and put the letter in the post. Then, he marched back home.

When Tim got home, his mom was happy. She said, "Good job, Tim! You listened and marched in a straight line." Tim felt proud. He learned that listening to mom is important. And that is the moral of the story: always listen to your mom.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear named Ben. Ben had a friend named Timmy, who was a little bunny. They loved to play together in the forest.

Just then, Jim heard some little feet running across the grass. He looked around and saw a little girl running towards him. She was only three years old, but she was strong. She got out some scissors and gently cut the strings. 

Jim was so happy to be free! He thanked the little girl and flew away. The little girl smiled as she watched him go and knew she had helped a frustrated chicken.

Once there was a little girl named Emily. She wanted to dream big. But every day, she felt sad and scared. She cried as she looked out of her window, feeling so lonely.

Then one day, a shining light appeared out of the clouds, lighting up the sky. In the light was a razor. Emily touched the razor, and immediately felt a surge of courage and joy.

She used the razor to cut away her sadness and fear. She felt free, like she could now dream.

Night after night, Emily would reach out and grab the razor and use it to dream. She journeyed to magical lands, made new friends, and felt like she could do anything.

But one night, the light was gone and the razor was dead. Emily was heartbroken, but she still remembered how to dream. She dreamt even bigger, as if nothing could stop her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was very worried. Something bad was coming and she could feel it.

She wanted to get away, so she started to run. She ran fast, as fast as she could. She wanted to get away before it got too close.

Her mommy urged her to hurry. She said "Run, run quickly! Don't worry, I'm right behind you."

The little girl kept running, urged on by her mommy's words. She felt scared, but she kept running.

Finally, she reached a safe place. She was safe. Her mommy hugged her tight.

They had made it in time. The little girl was no longer worried.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jenny. She loved to sing. One day, Jenny was singing with her mom. Then, she noticed something on the ground. It was a file! It was thick and blue.

Jenny picked it up and opened it. Inside, she found lots of music. She shouted with glee and started singing her favorite song.

Mom smiled and joined in. They danced around the room, singing at the top of their lungs. Then Mom picked up the file and said, "Let's sing all these songs together!"

Jenny and her mom sang and sang. They sang all day long and had so much fun.

When it was time to go, they took the thick file with them. Whenever they wanted to sing, they opened the file and found a new song. They sang and danced all the way home.

One day, Pete and Sam went to the top of the hill to talk. They watched the wild animals running around below them. They talked about how brave and strong the animals were. 

All of a sudden, there was a loud noise and a wild wind blew. Pete and Sam had to hold on tight to the top of the hill. The wind blew and blew and became wilder and wilder.

Finally, it stopped and Pete and Sam were safe. They decided to go back home to talk about their adventure. They were happy they had been brave and stayed at the top of the hill.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear. He had soft brown fur and lived in a poor village deep in the forest. All the animals knew how poor he was, and they all wanted to help.

One day, a big eagle flew into the village and dropped a gift for the little bear. It was a big sack of food. The food was so delicious and it soon spread around the village to all the animals.

The little bear was so excited! His fur shone brighter than ever and he ate and ate until all the food was gone.

Soon, everyone in the village was happy and full. And the little bear's fur was the softest and warmest it had ever been. All the village animals were very grateful to the eagle. 

The end.

Tommy and Mommy went outside to watch the sunset. Tommy was so happy to be outside. He saw the pretty colors in the sky. The sky was orange and pink like the ice cream he ate for dessert. 

Mommy pointed to the sun gradually sinking behind the trees. Tommy saw the yellow sun getting lower and lower. He yelled and pointed, "Look, Mommy, the sun is snapping!" 

Mommy laughed and hugged Tommy. She said, "Yes, the sun is giving us a beautiful sunset. It makes us so happy!" 

Tommy and Mommy watched the sunset until the sun was all gone. Then, they went back inside. Tommy smiled and said, "The sunset was so nice! I'm so happy!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She had long blonde hair and she loved wearing her pretty skirt. One day, Lucy was playing in the garden when she heard a noise coming from the bushes.

Curious, she went over to investigate and found a small puppy! It was a cute brown puppy with big floppy ears. Lucy was so excited, she couldn't help but speak to the puppy.

The puppy was very scared and it had been lost in the big garden for a while. So Lucy was very patient and slowly she sat down on the ground and talked to the puppy softly.

Slowly, the puppy came out of the bushes and began to listen to the little girl. They played together for hours and the puppy began to feel at home.

When Lucy got home, she spoke about the puppy to her mum. So the next day, her mum took Lucy back to the garden with a leash. The puppy recognised Lucy and bounded over to her.

And so, Lucy and the puppy became the best of friends!

Once upon a time, there was a bee who lived in a hive all by herself. She was very shy and never wanted to talk to anyone. One day, while she was sitting alone, the bee heard something whispering in the wind. It was a beautiful voice that the bee had never heard before.

The bee flew out of the hive to see who was talking. When she got outside, she couldn't see anyone. But then, she spotted a little girl standing in the grass. She was whispering a song that the bee had never heard before.

The bee was so fascinated by the song, she flew closer and tried to get a better look at the little girl. The girl was shy too, and when she saw the bee, she started to run away. But the bee followed her, still trying to listen and learn the song.

Eventually, the little girl stopped. She looked at the bee and then smiled. She kept whispering the song until the sun went down. Then, she skipped away, leaving the bee humming along to the memory of the song.

Once upon a time there was a vase. It was big and beautiful. The vase was loved by everyone and they admired it. But one day somebody made the vase very angry. They banged it and broke it. The vase was so angry it started to cry. Everyone was sad and didn't know what to do.

But then the little boy came. He was only three and he had a very special plan. He gathered some of the vase's pieces and put them together in the garden. He added pebbles, leaves and flowers and worked really hard to make the vase look better. 

When he had finished, the little boy showed it to everyone. Everyone was amazed. The vase was so beautiful once again! Everyone was so happy and the vase was no longer angry. 

The little boy had done a very good job. He was proud of himself. Everyone praised him and thanked him for making the vase happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. Lucy was a happy girl. She had a special mask that she liked to wear. It was pink and it made her feel like she was a princess. 

But one day, Lucy got mad at her mum. She started to complain. She shouted and said that she wanted to wear her mask all the time.

Her mum was so patient. She told Lucy that she couldn't wear her mask all the time, but she could wear it for a few hours each day. Lucy felt better and was happy again.

So, every day, Lucy would wear her princess mask for a few hours, and she was always happy when she could wear it. She would smile and laugh and she would never complain again.

Once there was a fragile train. It was full of special cars and it was gray. One day, the train was riding down the tracks. Suddenly, the engine started to rot. The train shook and stopped at a station. Everyone got off and looked at the rot. Nobody knew what had happened!

The train driver and engineer came to look at the rot. They looked closely, but couldn't fix it. Finally, the conductor said, "We need a new engine for this fragile train." Everyone nodded in agreement.

The next day, a new engine arrived at the station. Everyone cheered and the workers put it onto the train. After that, the fragile train started rolling down the tracks again. Everyone on the train was happy. They could go to their destination.

One day, a hungry little boy was walking through the park. He was looking around, hoping to find something to eat. Suddenly, he saw a hook hanging from a nearby tree. He ran over, and saw that it was holding a delicious apple. He reached up to grab the apple. But his little fingers were too short!

He looked around, thinking of a way to get the apple. Suddenly, he had an idea! He took off his shirt and used it to wipe the hook. He wiped and wiped until the hook was nice and clean.

He waited. Pretty soon, the hook started to move. He stepped back in surprise - it was working! The hook slowly moved down until it was at the perfect reaching height.

The grateful boy grabbed the apple, and happily ate it. He laughed and smiled, feeling very pleased with his clever plan.

Once upon a time, there was a poor orphan named Jack. He was so poor that he had no parents and no home. All he had was a shield. 
Every day, Jack carried his shield and walked around the city. He hoped that one day he would meet someone who would be compassionate and show him what true love felt like. 
Then one day, Jack stopped in front of a special house. It was the house of the King. He wanted to see what it was like inside.
As Jack was standing in front of the King's house, a kind old lady came out of the door and looked at him. She had a gentle smile on her face. She said, "What brings you here, little one?"
Jack was surprised. He told her his story and the old lady was so moved by his courage she decided to adopt him. She gave him a warm hug and said, "Welcome home, my son." 
Jack was so happy and surprised. From then on he lived in the King's house and received true love and compassion from the old lady. He thanked her every day for her kindness and kept his shield close to him for always.
